  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Joint completion/discrete-symmetry loci]\n\\label{p2d:cor:joint-completion-symmetry-loci}\nLet\n\\[\n \\mathfrak A_{\\rm coord}\n =\\{(r_L,r_R,\\varrho):\n       r_L,r_R,\\varrho\\in\\mathbb R_{\\geq0}\\}\n\\]\ndenote the unmarked level-one completion atlas.\n\\begin{enumerate}[label=(\\roman*),leftmargin=2.2em]\n\\item If parity is only required to act covariantly on the completion family,\nthe licensed output is the graph\n\\[\n \\Gamma_{\\mathcal P}\n =\\{(c,\\mathcal P c):c\\in\\mathfrak A_{\\rm coord}\\},\n \\qquad\n \\mathcal P(r_L,r_R,\\varrho)=(r_R,r_L,\\varrho).\n\\]\nProjection onto \\(c\\) is a bijection, so covariance selects no completion.\n\\item If an independently generated claim requires the \\emph{same} unmarked\ncompletion class to be parity fixed, the joint zero-defect locus is the fibre\nproduct of \\(\\Gamma_{\\mathcal P}\\) with the diagonal:\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\mathfrak Z_{\\mathcal P}\n =\\{(r,r,\\varrho):r,\\varrho\\in\\mathbb R_{\\geq0}\\}.}\n\\]\nThe crossed classes \\(r_L\\neq r_R\\) survive the coordinate classification\nseparately but have nonzero joint relation defect for this same-completion\nclaim.\n\\item At level one, time reversal fixes every unmarked completion class.\nConsequently its same-completion locus is\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\mathfrak Z_{\\mathcal T}=\\mathfrak A_{\\rm coord}.}\n\\]\nRequiring literal equality of a phase-marked representative with a chosen\nanti-unitary lift is a stronger implementation relation and cannot be inserted\ninto this quotient-level locus.\n\\end{enumerate}\nIntersecting the parity-fixed locus with Paper~II-C's least-closure graph\nremoves the two one-adjoint-channel branches: for \\(r=0\\) the least closure of\n\\(\\mathcal E_9\\) is \\(\\mathcal E_9\\), while for \\(r>0\\) it is\n\\(\\mathcal H_1\\).  This is a joint compatibility statement, not a new carrier\nor completion selector.\n\\end{corollary}",
  "proof": {

      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",

    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe proposition above gives the two actions on quotient coordinates.  A\ngenerated readout \\(c\\mapsto\\mathcal Pc\\) produces its graph, whose first\nprojection has inverse \\(c\\mapsto(c,\\mathcal Pc)\\).  Imposing equality of its\ntwo entries gives \\(r_L=r_R\\) and no condition on \\(\\varrho\\).  Time reversal\nacts trivially on the level-one quotient, giving the full atlas.  Finally,\nPaper~II-C's coordinate/closure theorem adds one adjoint target for each\nnonzero one of \\(r_L,r_R\\); on the diagonal they vanish together or occur\ntogether, proving the last statement.\n\\end{proof}"

On the finite non-diagonal \\(\\Spin(4)\\)-module the Cartan\nrepresentative provides a useful weight atlas. BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-002 — E1

{
  "claim_id": "p2:def:finite-diagonal-spin-weight-hopf-charge",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0058",
  "source_label": "p2:def:finite-diagonal-spin-weight-hopf-charge",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 2094,
    "line_end": 2132,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{definition}[Finite diagonal spin weight and geometric Hopf charge]\n\\label{p2:def:finite-diagonal-spin-weight-hopf-charge}\nOn \\(\\mathcal H_m\\), after fixing a diagonal Cartan axis, define\n\\[\n \\widehat{\\mathfrak s}:=L_3^++L_3^-=\\widehat J_3/\\hbar,\\qquad\n \\mathfrak s=m_L+m_R\\in\\tfrac12\\ZZ,\\qquad\n -m\\le\\mathfrak s\\le m.\n\\]\nHere \\(m_L,m_R\\) denote the weights of the existing algebraic generators\n\\(L_3^+,L_3^-\\), respectively.\n\nFor the chosen geometric left-fibre action\n\\(g\\mapsto h_\\alpha g\\), \\(h_\\alpha=\\exp(i\\alpha\\sigma_3)\\), set\n\\[\n \\widehat{\\mathfrak h}:=Q_{H,L}\n =-i\\Rmom\\xi=-2i\\partial_\\psi=-2L_3^-,\n \\qquad \\psi=2\\alpha,\\qquad \\psi\\sim\\psi+4\\pi.\n\\]\nEquivalently,\n\\[\n U_L(\\alpha)f(g)=f(h_\\alpha g),\\qquad\n U_L(\\alpha)=e^{i\\alpha Q_{H,L}}=e^{-2i\\alpha L_3^-}.\n\\]\nFor \\(D^j_{ab}(g)=\\langle a|\\rho_j(g)|b\\rangle\\),\n\\[\n D^j_{ab}(h_\\alpha g)=e^{2ia\\alpha}D^j_{ab}(g),\\qquad\n D^j_{ab}(gh_\\alpha)=e^{2ib\\alpha}D^j_{ab}(g).\n\\]\nConsequently\n\\[\n \\boxed{m_L=b,\\qquad m_R=-a,\\qquad q=q_L=-2m_R=2a,}\n \\qquad q_R=2m_L=2b.\n\\]\nThe diagonal weight on these scalar matrix coefficients is\n\\(\\mathfrak s=b-a\\).  It generates the diagonal subgroup, represented\ngeometrically by conjugation, and is distinct from the chosen left\nHopf-fibre charge.  The integer character is \\(e^{iq\\alpha}\\), or\n\\(e^{iq\\psi/2}\\) in the \\(4\\pi\\)-periodic parameter.\n\\end{definition}",
  "proof": null,
  "kind": "DEFINITION",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-002",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "FORMALIZED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "L+ andL- weightsmL,mR; geometric multiplication-side dictionary from batch2."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "From the existing geometric-side dictionary, Q_HL=-2L3-=-2i partial_psi. The diagonal rotation weight is mL+mR and has absolute value at most jL+jR<=m.",
    "Left and right multiplication of D_ab give phases exp(2ia alpha) and exp(2ib alpha). Hence mR=-a, mL=b, qL=2a, qR=2b and s=b-a. The factor of two agrees with both angle periods."
  ],
  "conditions_proposed": [

  ],

BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-003 — E1

{
  "claim_id": "p2d:prop:coordinate-hopf-charge-steps",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0059",
  "source_label": "p2d:prop:coordinate-hopf-charge-steps",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 2134,
    "line_end": 2157,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Coordinate Hopf-charge steps and the superselection boundary]\n\\label{p2d:prop:coordinate-hopf-charge-steps}\nFix the oriented left-fibre representative of\nDefinition~\\ref{p2:def:finite-diagonal-spin-weight-hopf-charge} and write\n\\(Q_H:=Q_{H,L}=-2L_3^-\\).  The complexification of any equivariant\ncoordinate tuple of type \\((\\tfrac12,\\tfrac12)\\) admits components\n\\(X_{\\pm,\\alpha}\\), \\(\\alpha=1,2\\), such that\n\\[\n \\boxed{[Q_H,X_{\\pm,\\alpha}]=\\pm X_{\\pm,\\alpha},\\qquad\n P_qX_{\\pm,\\alpha}P_r=0\\quad\\text{unless }q=r\\pm1,}\n\\]\nwhere \\(P_q\\) are the spectral projectors of \\(Q_H\\) on the retained\ncarrier.  The same identities hold under every equivariant finite\ncompression.  These coordinate components preserve the diagonal central\nparity \\(\\Gamma_c\\) of Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:diagonal-center-grading}.\nThus Hopf grading and central parity impose different selection rules.\n\nIn particular, the nonzero intrinsic coordinate tuple does not lie in\n\\(\\{Q_H\\}'\\).  A Hopf-weight decomposition alone therefore does not\nestablish charge superselection for an accessible algebra containing that\ntuple.  The charge-invariant accessible algebra and dynamical stability\nrequired by Paper~IV, Corollary~\\ref{p4:cor:hopf-reeb-superselection},\nremain the appropriate additional conditions.\n\\end{proposition}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2159,
      "line_end": 2172,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe right spin-\\(\\tfrac12\\) factor of the coordinate representation has\n\\(-2L_3^-\\)-weights \\(\\pm1\\); its other spin-\\(\\tfrac12\\) factor\nsupplies the index \\(\\alpha\\).  Differentiating coordinate covariance\ngives the displayed commutator.  Multiplication on the left and right by\n\\(P_q,P_r\\) gives\n\\((q-r\\mp1)P_qX_{\\pm,\\alpha}P_r=0\\), proving the selection rule.\nAn equivariant compression projector commutes with \\(Q_H\\), so compression\npreserves the commutator exactly.  Central-evenness is the existing\ncoordinate-type calculation in Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:diagonal-center-grading}.\nIf every component commuted with \\(Q_H\\), the commutator identities would\nforce the entire tuple to vanish.  The intrinsic tuple is nonzero, giving\nthe final claim.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "PROPOSITION",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-003",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "Coordinate representation(1/2,1/2),Q_H=-2L3-, spectral projectorsP_q and an equivariant finite compression."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "The coordinate representation has Q_H weights +1 and -1, each twice. Differentiated covariance gives the commutator and sandwiching by charge projectors gives q=r+/-1.",
    "An equivariant cutoff commutes with Q_H and preserves this identity. Coordinates remain central even because their two endpoint central characters agree.",
    "A nonzero coordinate tuple cannot commute with Q_H, since none of its coordinate weights is zero. The later superselection theorem requires an actual charge-commuting accessible algebra and appropriate channel covariance; grading alone does not suffice."
  ],
  "conditions_proposed": [
    "Equivariant coordinate tuple; nonzero intrinsic tuple for the final accessible-algebra claim.",
    "Superselection would require its actual accessible algebra and dynamical stability, not assumed here."
  ],
  "import_labels": [
    "p2:thm:diagonal-center-grading",
    "p4:cor:hopf-reeb-superselection"
  ],

  "id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-003",
  "target": "p2d:prop:coordinate-hopf-charge-steps"
}

BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-004 — E1

{
  "claim_id": "p2d:rem:hopf-charge-versus-transverse-shell-degree",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0060",
  "source_label": "p2d:rem:hopf-charge-versus-transverse-shell-degree",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 2175,
    "line_end": 2195,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{remark}[Hopf fibre charge, diagonal weight, and transverse-shell degree]\n\\label{p2d:rem:hopf-charge-versus-transverse-shell-degree}\nThree labels that live on the same marked round geometry have different\nrepresentation-theoretic meanings and are not identified.  The geometric\nHopf charge \\(q\\) above is the character of the selected one-sided fibre\n\\(U(1)\\).  The number \\(\\mathfrak s\\) is a Cartan weight for the diagonal\nrotation subgroup acting by conjugation.  By contrast, the transverse-shell\nlabel \\(\\ell\\) in the Paper~I-A/II-C shell-symbol theorem\n\\[\n E_k^x\\simeq\\bigoplus_{\\ell=0}^{k}\\mathscr Y_\\ell(S_H^2)\n\\]\nlabels the irreducible diagonal-rotation \\(SU(2)\\) type itself; within one\nsuch \\(V_\\ell\\), its Cartan weights range from \\(-\\ell\\) to \\(+\\ell\\).\nAccordingly, neither \\(\\ell=q\\) nor \\(\\ell=\\mathfrak s\\) is generated by the\nframework.  The shell-symbol map is also not ordinary Hopf pullback:\nordinary fibre-basic pullback obeys\n\\(\\pi^*\\mathscr Y_\\ell(S_H^2)\\subset E_{2\\ell}(S^3)\\), whereas the\nHopf-marked diagonal symbolization reconstructs the full shell \\(E_k\\) as the\ncomplete window \\(0\\le\\ell\\le k\\).  This firewall prevents the transverse\nfrontier rank from being reinterpreted as a Hopf-charge count.\n\\end{remark}",

{
  "claim_id": "p2:prop:diagonal-spin-weight-sector-decomposition",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0061",
  "source_label": "p2:prop:diagonal-spin-weight-sector-decomposition",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 2197,
    "line_end": 2207,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Diagonal spin-weight sector decomposition]\n\\label{p2:prop:diagonal-spin-weight-sector-decomposition}\nThe Hilbert space decomposes into finite diagonal spin-weight sectors:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\mathcal H_m=\\bigoplus_{\\mathfrak s\\in \\frac12\\ZZ,\\ |\\mathfrak s|\\le m}\\mathcal H_m^{(\\mathfrak s)},\n\\qquad\n\\mathcal H_m^{(\\mathfrak s)}\n=\n\\{\\psi\\in\\mathcal H_m:\\hat{\\mathfrak s}\\psi=\\mathfrak s\\psi\\}.\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{proposition}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2209,
      "line_end": 2215,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nSince \\(\\hat{\\mathfrak s}\\) is Hermitian, \\(\\mathcal H_m\\) decomposes as the orthogonal direct sum of its eigenspaces:\n\\[\n\\mathcal H_m=\\bigoplus_{\\mathfrak s}\\ker(\\hat{\\mathfrak s}-\\mathfrak s\\mathbf 1).\n\\]\nThis is exactly the stated decomposition.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "PROPOSITION",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-005",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "Finite-dimensionalH_m and Hermitian diagonal Cartan generator."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "The finite Hermitian generator decomposes orthogonally by the spectral theorem. Its tensor-product weights are half-integral and satisfy |mL+mR|<=jL+jR<=m.",
    "This is a diagonal-weight decomposition, not a scalar Hopf-charge decomposition."
  ],
  "conditions_proposed": [],

    "p2:def:finite-diagonal-spin-weight-hopf-charge"
  ],

{
  "claim_id": "p2:prop:hopf-class-existence-nonselection",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0064",
  "source_label": "p2:prop:hopf-class-existence-nonselection",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 2254,
    "line_end": 2270,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Hopf-fibration existence, conjugacy, and nonselection]\n\\label{p2:prop:hopf-class-existence-nonselection}\nLet \\(G\\simeq SU(2)\\) be the constituted nonabelian transfer parent.  Every\nmaximal torus \\(T\\subset G\\) satisfies\n\\[\n        T\\simeq U(1),\n        \\qquad\n        T\\backslash G\\simeq S^2,\n\\]\nand the left-orbit quotient map \\(G\\to T\\backslash G\\) is a Hopf fibration\n(equivalently one may use \\(G/T\\) after inversion).  All maximal tori are\nconjugate, so these fibrations form one equivalence class after a handedness\nhas been fixed, but no particular \\(T\\) is invariant under all inner\nautomorphisms of \\(G\\).  The parent geometry therefore determines the Hopf\nconjugacy class and its choice-independent invariants, but no preferred embedded\nfiber circle.\n\\end{proposition}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2272,
      "line_end": 2280,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nExistence and \\(T\\backslash G\\simeq S^2\\) are the rank-one homogeneous-space\ndescription \\(U(1)\\backslash SU(2)\\simeq S^2\\), equivalent under inversion to\n\\(SU(2)/U(1)\\simeq S^2\\).  The conjugacy theorem for maximal tori\nshows that any two choices are related by an inner automorphism.  If one torus\nwere selected by the unmarked parent, it would be characteristic.  This is\nimpossible because conjugation acts transitively and nontrivially on the\nmaximal tori of \\(SU(2)\\).  Hence only the orbit of choices is endogenous.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "PROPOSITION",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-008",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "Constituted parentSU(2) and maximal torusT."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "A maximal torus of SU(2) is U(1); its free left quotient is S2, giving the Hopf fibration. All maximal tori are conjugate.",
    "The adjoint action moves a Cartan axis nontrivially, so no particular torus is invariant under every inner automorphism. The unmarked parent determines the orbit of choices and its invariants, not a preferred embedded fibre."
  ],
  "conditions_proposed": [],
  "import_labels": [
    "p2:thm:single-su2-derived-spin4-isometries",

  ],

{
  "claim_id": "p2:thm:forced-hopf-chern-unit",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0066",
  "source_label": "p2:thm:forced-hopf-chern-unit",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 2292,
    "line_end": 2308,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Chern unit of a Hopf representative on the simply connected parent]\n\\label{p2:thm:forced-hopf-chern-unit}\nLet\n\\[\n        U(1)\\longrightarrow P\\longrightarrow S^2\n\\]\nbe any principal-circle representative whose total space is the constituted\nsimply connected parent \\(P\\simeq S^3\\).  Then its first Chern class satisfies\n\\[\n|c_1(P)|=1.\n\\]\nAfter the Hopf/base orientation convention is fixed, the chosen oriented\nrepresentative may be written\n\\[\nc_1(P)=+1.\n\\]\n\\end{theorem}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2310,
      "line_end": 2327,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nPrincipal \\(U(1)\\)-bundles over \\(S^2\\) are classified by\n\\(c_1(P)=k\\in\\mathbb Z\\).  The homotopy exact sequence contains\n\\[\n \\pi_2(S^2)\\cong\\mathbb Z\n \\xrightarrow{\\ \\times k\\ }\n \\pi_1(U(1))\\cong\\mathbb Z\n \\longrightarrow\\pi_1(P)\\longrightarrow0.\n\\]\nConsequently \\(\\pi_1(P)\\cong\\mathbb Z/k\\mathbb Z\\), with the \\(k=0\\)\ncase interpreted as \\(\\mathbb Z\\).  Since \\(P\\simeq S^3\\) is simply\nconnected, \\(|k|=1\\).  The two signs are exchanged by reversing either the fibre orientation or\nthe base orientation, with the other held fixed; simultaneous reversal of\nboth preserves \\(k\\).  Indeed,\n\\(k=\\langle c_1(P),[S^2]\\rangle\\), and these two reversals negate\n\\(c_1(P)\\) and \\([S^2]\\), respectively.  With the Paper-I-A oriented\nrepresentative, \\(k=+1\\).\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "THEOREM",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-010",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "PrincipalU(1) bundle overS2 with total spaceP~S3; classifyingChern numberk."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "The bundle homotopy sequence gives Z --times k--> Z ->pi1(P)->0. Its cokernel is Z/kZ, with k=0 giving Z. Simple connectedness of P=S3 therefore forces |k|=1.",
    "Reversing either fibre or base orientation alone reverses the evaluated Chern number; reversing both preserves it. The chosen I-A orientation gives +1. This does not select an associated matter charge."
  ],
  "conditions_proposed": [
    "Principal-circle bundle and stated total-space topology; orientation only for the sign."
  ],

  ],

  "source_as_printed": "Fix the chosen left-fiber Paper-I-A representative of this conjugacy class.\nLet\n\\[\n\\eta_0:=\\eta/\\Rmom\n\\]\nbe its dimensionless principal \\(U(1)\\)-connection.  The bundle is\n\\[\n\\Sone\\hookrightarrow S^3(\\Rmom)\\longrightarrow S^2.\n\\]\nThen\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{p2:eq:eta0}\n\\oint_{S^1}\\eta_0=2\\pi,\n\\qquad\n d\\eta_0=\\pi^*\\omega,\n\\qquad\n\\frac{1}{2\\pi}\\int_{S^2}\\omega = 1,\n\\end{equation}\nso \\(c_1(P)=1\\).   "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{definition}[Abelian Chern--Simons diagnostic on the total space]\n\\label{p2:def:cs-charge}\nFor a real one-form \\(A\\) on \\(S^3\\), define the quadratic abelian\nChern--Simons diagnostic\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{p2:eq:cs}\nQ_{\\CS}[A] \\;:=\\; \\frac{1}{4\\pi^2}\\int_{S^3} A\\wedge dA.\n\\end{equation}\nWhen \\(A=\\eta_0\\), this is evaluated on the principal Hopf connection.  When\n\\(A=q\\eta_0\\) with \\(q\\ne1\\), it is evaluated on the pullback of the\nconnection induced on the associated character line; \\(q\\eta_0\\) is not a\nnew principal connection on the same circle bundle because its vertical\nnormalization is \\(q\\), not \\(1\\).\n\\end{definition}",
  "proof": null,
  "kind": "DEFINITION",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-013",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "FORMALIZED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "Realone-formA on the closedorientedS3."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "The expression Q_CS[A]=(4pi^2)^-1 integral A wedge dA is a quadratic diagnostic for a real one-form on oriented S3. No integrality is asserted for arbitrary forms.",
    "The vertical value of q eta0 is q. For q!=1 it is not a principal connection on the same principal circle bundle; it is the pulled-back induced associated-line connection."
  ],
  "conditions_proposed": [
    "Chosen totalorientation and displayedabelian normalization."

{
  "claim_id": "p2:prop:hopfion-charge",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0070",
  "source_label": "p2:prop:hopfion-charge",
  "source": {

    "line_end": 2432,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Principal and associated-character normalizations]\n\\label{p2:prop:hopfion-charge}\nAmong the homogeneous scalar multiples \\(s\\eta_0\\), the form \\(\\eta_0\\) is\nthe unique one with the principal normalization\n\\((s\\eta_0)(\\xi_0)=1\\).  It represents the homogeneous Reeb-normalized principal-connection gauge\nclass and satisfies\n\\(\nQ_{\\CS}[\\eta_0]=1.\n\\)\nFor the integer character\n\\(\\rho_q(e^{i\\alpha})=e^{iq\\alpha}\\), let\n\\[\n        L^q:=S^3\\times_{\\rho_q}\\mathbb C\\longrightarrow S^2.\n\\]\nThe induced associated-line connection has, after pullback to \\(S^3\\),\n\\begin{equation}\n\\label{p2:eq:Aq0-q0eta0}\nA_q=q\\,\\eta_0-d\\chi,\n\\qquad q\\in\\ZZ,\n\\end{equation}\nand its curvature and first Chern class are\n\\[\n        F_q=q\\,\\omega,\n        \\qquad\n        c_1(L^q)=\\frac{[F_q]}{2\\pi}=q.\n\\]\nIts total-space quadratic diagnostic is\n\\(Q_{\\CS}[A_q]=q^2\\).\n\nThe arbitrary-real one-form diagnostic and the conditional global homogeneous\nBerry normalization are supplementary and are recorded in\nPaper~II-F, Section~\\ref{p2d:app:berry-technical} after their exact hypotheses.\n\\end{proposition}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2434,
      "line_end": 2457,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nFor a homogeneous scalar multiple \\(s\\eta_0\\), the principal vertical\nnormalization is\n\\((s\\eta_0)(\\xi_0)=s\\), so it forces \\(s=1\\).  This uniqueness statement is\nonly within the homogeneous scalar-multiple family; it does not exclude\ndistinct gauge-related principal connections such as\n\\(\\eta_0-\\pi^*d\\bar\\chi\\) for a smooth real function\n\\(\\bar\\chi\\) on \\(S^2\\) with \\(d\\bar\\chi\\not\\equiv0\\).\nUsing \\eqref{p2:eq:eta0} and fiber integration directly in the main proof gives\n\\[\n \\int_{S^3}\\eta_0\\wedge d\\eta_0\n =\\int_{S^2}\\!\\left(\\oint_{S^1}\\eta_0\\right)\\omega\n =(2\\pi)(2\\pi)=4\\pi^2,\n\\]\nand hence \\(Q_{\\CS}[\\eta_0]=1\\) in the convention\n\\eqref{p2:eq:cs}.  Applying the character differential\n\\(d\\rho_q:q\\) to the principal connection and curvature gives\n\\(A_q=q\\eta_0-d\\chi\\) and \\(F_q=q\\omega\\); hence\n\\(c_1(L^q)=q[\\omega/(2\\pi)]=q\\).  For\n\\(A_s=s\\eta_0-d\\chi\\), the exact gauge term integrates to zero on closed\n\\(S^3\\), so quadratic scaling gives\n\\(Q_{\\CS}[A_s]=s^2\\).  Applying this with \\(s=q\\) proves the associated-line\nclaim.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "PROPOSITION",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-014",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "eta0(xi0)=1, fibreintegral2pi,deta0=pi*omega,baseintegral2pi; inducedcharacterconnection forintegerq."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "Among scalar multiples s eta0, principal vertical normalization forces s=1. The source expressly limits this uniqueness to that family and allows gauge-related exact horizontal terms.",
    "Fibre integration gives integral eta0 wedge d eta0=(2pi)(2pi)=4pi^2 and Q_CS[eta0]=1 in the declared orientation.",
    "The character differential multiplies connection and curvature by q. Thus A_q=q eta0-dchi, F_q=q omega and c1(L^q)=q. The sign matches the explicit I-A left-equivariance convention.",
    "The gauge cross-term is -q d(chi d eta0), whose integral vanishes on closed S3. Every global U(1) phase on S3 has a global real lift because H1(S3;Z)=0. Hence Q_CS[A_q]=q^2 with no omitted large gauge class."
  ],
  "conditions_proposed": [

  ],

{
  "claim_id": "p2d:cor:associated-character-readout-graph",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0071",
  "source_label": "p2d:cor:associated-character-readout-graph",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 2459,
    "line_end": 2480,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Associated-character readout graph and nonselection]\n\\label{p2d:cor:associated-character-readout-graph}\nModulo gauge on the pulled-back connection, the complete generated\nassociated-character package is the graph\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n \\Gamma_{\\rm char}\n =\n \\left\\{\n \\left(q,\\,[q\\eta_0],\\,q\\omega,\\,q,\\,q^2\\right):\n q\\in\\mathbb Z\n \\right\\},}\n\\]\nwhere the entries after \\(q\\) are respectively the pulled-back connection\nclass, curvature, first Chern number, and total-space quadratic diagnostic.\nProjection \\(\\Gamma_{\\rm char}\\to\\mathbb Z\\) is a bijection.  Thus curvature,\nChern number, and Chern--Simons readouts co-realize with the character and\ncannot by themselves select \\(q\\).  An independently generated associated-line\nChern requirement \\(c_1(L^q)=n\\) instead forms a fibre product and fixes\n\\(q=n\\); the principal-bundle statement \\(c_1(P)=1\\) is differently typed and\ndoes not supply that relation.\n\\end{corollary}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2482,
      "line_end": 2490,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nProposition~\\ref{p2:prop:hopfion-charge} gives every component as a function of\n\\(q\\), and the first component recovers \\(q\\), proving that the package is a\ngraph isomorphic to the integer atlas.  Intersecting it with the\nassociated-line equation \\(c_1=n\\) gives \\(q=n\\).  The principal Chern class\nbelongs to the principal bundle rather than to a chosen associated line, so\nthe typed cross-relation firewall forbids replacing the latter equation by\n\\(c_1(P)=1\\).\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "COROLLARY",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-015",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,

    "Each q determines its connection class, curvature, Chern number and quadratic diagnostic. Retaining q as the first graph entry makes projection onto the integer atlas a bijection, so the graph eliminates no charge.",
    "A separate associated-line Chern condition c1(L^q)=n gives q=n. Substituting the differently typed principal condition c1(P)=1 would be an unlicensed cross-relation."

  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{remark}[Normalization and interpretation boundary]\n\\label{p2:rem:hopf-normalization-conversion}\nThe integer character \\(q\\) and the projected ray weight\n\\(r\\in\\frac12\\mathbb Z\\) are independent labels.  The associated-line Chern\nclass is linear and oriented, whereas a total-space Chern--Simons diagnostic\nis quadratic and loses the sign.  A projected half-integral \\(r\\) is\ndouble-cover/local lift data; only an integer \\(r\\) can occur in the global\nhomogeneous Berry form under the present \\(2\\pi\\) principal normalization.\nThe chosen form \\(B_r=r\\eta_0\\) exists for arbitrary real \\(r\\), but its\nquadratic diagnostic must not be promoted to a global Berry invariant without\na separate global ray-and-connection construction.  No physical charge\nidentification or superselection statement follows in Paper~II.\n\\end{remark}",

  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "We use the Hopf/contact normalization established in Paper~I-A \\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  Thus the Hopf fibration \\(\\Sone \\hookrightarrow S^3 \\xrightarrow{\\pi} S^2\\) realizes $S^3(\\Rmom)$ as a principal $\\mathrm{U}(1)$-bundle over the symplectic manifold $(S^2(\\Rmom/2),\\omega)$. Let $\\vol_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)}$ denote the Riemannian area form, so $\\int_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)}\\vol_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)}=\\pi \\Rmom^2$. We take the normalized symplectic form\n\\[\n\\omega := \\frac{2}{\\Rmom^2}\\,\\vol_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)},\\qquad \\int_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)}\\omega = 2\\pi,\n\\]\nso that the associated complex line bundle $L\\to S^2(\\Rmom/2)$ has $c_1(L)=[\\omega]/(2\\pi)=1$.\n",

  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Hopf connection and prequantum bundle]\n\\label{p2:prop:hopf-connection-prequantum-bundle}\nLet $\\eta_0$ denote the \\emph{dimensionless} principal $\\mathrm{U}(1)$-connection 1-form on the Hopf bundle $S^3\\to S^2$, with principal generator $\\xi_0$ normalized by $\\eta_0(\\xi_0)=1$, and set\n\\[\n\\eta := \\Rmom\\,\\eta_0,\n\\qquad\n\\xi:=\\Rmom^{-1}\\xi_0.\n\\]\nThe metric-scaled contact form is normalized by $\\eta(\\xi)=1$.\nThen the curvature of the principal connection is \\cite{blair2010contact,boyer2008sasakian}\n\\[\nd\\eta_0 = \\pi^* \\omega,\n\\]\nso \\((S^3, \\eta_0)\\) is a prequantum circle bundle over \\((S^2, \\omega)\\) with integer Chern class \\(c_1 = 1\\).\n\\end{proposition}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2539,
      "line_end": 2543,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nPaper~I-A proves this degree-one Boothby--Wang normalization\n\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  The displayed equations translate its physical and\ndimensionless connections into Paper-II notation.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "PROPOSITION",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-018",

  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,

  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Generated principal/metric Hopf normalization graph]\n\\label{p2d:cor:generated-hopf-normalization-graph}\nFix the occurring round radius \\(\\Rmom>0\\), the \\(2\\pi\\)-periodic principal\ngenerator \\(\\xi_0\\), and its principal connection \\(\\eta_0\\) with\n\\(\\eta_0(\\xi_0)=1\\).  The metric normalization is the generated transport\ngraph\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n \\xi=\\Rmom^{-1}\\xi_0,\\qquad\n \\eta=\\Rmom\\eta_0,\\qquad\n \\eta(\\xi)=1,\\qquad\n d\\eta=\\Rmom\\,\\pi^*\\omega.}\n\\]\nThe metric generator, metric contact form, and their curvature are\nnonredundant outputs of the same normalization dictionary and co-realize with\nthe principal data.  They are not independent members requiring separate\nselectors.  Conversely, this graph does not select \\(\\Rmom\\), a maximal-torus\nrepresentative, an associated character, or a physical matter charge.\n\\end{corollary}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2565,
      "line_end": 2575,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe first two identities are the declared principal-to-metric transport.\nSubstitution gives\n\\(\\eta(\\xi)=(\\Rmom\\eta_0)(\\Rmom^{-1}\\xi_0)=1\\), and constancy of\n\\(\\Rmom\\) on the round host gives\n\\(d\\eta=\\Rmom\\,d\\eta_0=\\Rmom\\,\\pi^*\\omega\\).\nOmitting any declared output gives a closure defect once the dictionary is\nlicensed; multiplying either output by an additional free scalar changes the\ngenerated normalization relation.  The remaining quantities occupy distinct\nowner or associated-line slots and therefore are not fixed by this graph.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "COROLLARY",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-019",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,

{
  "claim_id": "p2:def:hopf-charge",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0076",

    "line_end": 2623,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{definition}[Integer Hopf charge in the $4\\pi$ fiber convention]\n\\label{p2:def:hopf-charge}\nLet $\\psi\\sim\\psi+4\\pi$ be the standard Hopf fiber angle on\n$S^3\\cong SU(2)$, so that the chosen left-fiber Hopf action is\n\\[\n g\\longmapsto h_\\theta g,\n \\qquad\n h_\\theta:=\\exp(i\\theta\\sigma_3/2),\n \\qquad \\theta\\sim\\theta+4\\pi.\n\\]\nThe Reeb vector field $\\xi = \\frac{2}{\\Rmom}\\partial_\\psi$ generates this fiber action on $S^3(\\Rmom)$. A field $\\phi \\in C^\\infty(S^3)$ has \\textbf{integer Hopf charge} $q \\in \\ZZ$ if\n\\begin{equation}\n\\partial_\\psi \\phi = i\\frac{q}{2}\\,\\phi,\n\\qquad\n\\xi(\\phi)=\\frac{i q}{\\Rmom}\\,\\phi,\n\\qquad\n\\phi(h_\\theta g)=e^{i(q/2)\\theta}\\phi(g).\n\\label{p2:eq:hopf-charge-convention}\n\\end{equation}\nEquivalently, if one uses the $2\\pi$-periodic principal-$U(1)$ parameter $\\alpha=\\theta/2$, the character is $e^{iq\\alpha}$.  The Hilbert space decomposes as $L^2(S^3) = \\bigoplus_{q \\in \\ZZ} \\mathcal{V}_q$, where $\\mathcal{V}_q$ consists of charge-$q$ fields.\n\\end{definition}",
  "proof": null,
  "kind": "DEFINITION",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-020",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "FORMALIZED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "4pi-periodicanglepsi/theta, leftmultiplicationexp(i theta sigma3/2),Reebxi=2partialpsi/R."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "The differential eigenvalue condition partial_psi phi=iq phi/2, the Reeb condition xi phi=iq phi/R and the displayed equivariance law are equivalent. The 4pi period forces q to be integral.",
    "Changing to alpha=theta/2 gives exp(iq alpha), matching the previous principal-circle convention. The resulting compact-circle decomposition is of scalar parent L2, not the full finite non-diagonal module."
  ],

  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{remark}[Geometric interpretation and notation]\nCharge-$q$ fields are sections of the line bundle $L^q \\to S^2$, where\n$L$ is the degree-one bundle associated to the chosen left-fiber Hopf\nrepresentative. The case $q = 0$ corresponds to functions on the base $S^2$\npulled back to $S^3$; $q \\neq 0$ corresponds to genuinely ``twisted'' fields\nthat cannot be defined on $S^2$ alone.  Throughout this section, $q$ denotes\nthe integer geometric Hopf charge and $q/2$ is the exponent of its\nleft-fiber character in the \\(4\\pi\\) parameter.  This exponent is not\nidentified with the projected Berry label \\(r\\), and both are distinct from\nthe finite diagonal spin weight $\\mathfrak s$ used in the preceding\nfinite-module projector notation.\n\\end{remark}",
  "proof": null,

    "The q=0 fields are basic pullbacks. Nonzero q gives sections of a twisted line rather than ordinary base functions. The exponent q/2 is not the projected Berry label or the diagonal Cartan weight."

BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-023 — E1

{
  "claim_id": "p2d:cor:joint-hopf-charge-discrete-symmetry",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0079",
  "source_label": "p2d:cor:joint-hopf-charge-discrete-symmetry",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 2648,
    "line_end": 2676,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Joint charge/time-reversal and parity covariance]\n\\label{p2d:cor:joint-hopf-charge-discrete-symmetry}\nFor the chosen left-fibre charge atlas\n\\(\\{\\mathcal V_q\\}_{q\\in\\mathbb Z}\\), time reversal generates\n\\[\n \\mathcal T:\\mathcal V_q\\longrightarrow\\mathcal V_{-q}.\n\\]\nHence the complete time-reversal-covariant orbit of a nonzero charge is the\npair \\(\\mathcal V_q\\oplus\\mathcal V_{-q}\\); retaining both generated\nconstituents is co-realization, not a choice between them.  The joint locus for\na claim that one \\emph{single} charge sector is itself time-reversal fixed is\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\{q\\in\\mathbb Z:q=-q\\}=\\{0\\}.}\n\\]\nConsequently the simultaneous requirements \\(q\\neq0\\) and one\ntime-reversal-fixed charge sector have empty joint zero-defect locus.  GP3\ncannot repair that empty locus; a nonzero time-reversal-covariant package must\ncontain the opposite-charge pair (or additional typed sectors supplied by a\nlater constructor).\n\nSpatial parity transports the chosen left-fibre action with\n\\(\\mathcal P Q_{H,L}\\mathcal P^{-1}=-Q_{H,R}\\), so\n\\(\\mathcal P:\\mathcal V_q^L\\to\\mathcal V_{-q}^R\\).\nIt therefore generates a left/right covariance orbit, not\nan endomorphism of one fixed left-fibre sector and not a selector of a charge\nsign.  A parity-invariant charged claim must supply the corresponding\nleft/right pair or another independently generated bridge identifying the\nrelevant typed actions.\n\\end{corollary}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2678,
      "line_end": 2686,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:time-reversal-action} gives \\(q\\mapsto-q\\).\nThe orbit has one member exactly when \\(q=-q\\) in \\(\\mathbb Z\\), which forces\n\\(q=0\\); its intersection with \\(\\mathbb Z\\setminus\\{0\\}\\) is empty.\nThe parity clause is the left-to-right action proved in\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:parity-action}.  Since the target fibre action is differently\ntyped, the typed cross-relation firewall forbids treating that transport as\ncharge-sign selection inside the original left-fibre atlas.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "COROLLARY",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-023",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [

  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "Time reversal sends V_q to V_-q. A nonzero covariant orbit therefore contains the pair; a single fixed sector requires q=-q and hence q=0.",

    "Parity sends V_q^L to V_-q^R because it transports the left action to the negative right action. It does not act as an intrinsic charge-sign selector within one fixed left atlas."
  ],

BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-024 — E1

{
  "claim_id": "p2:lem:hopf-charge-selection-rule",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0080",
  "source_label": "p2:lem:hopf-charge-selection-rule",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 2690,
    "line_end": 2705,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{lemma}[Integer Hopf-charge selection rule]\n\\label{p2:lem:hopf-charge-selection-rule}\nIn the scalar Peter--Weyl sector with matrix coefficients \\(D^j_{ab}\\), the\nchosen left-fiber Hopf action gives integer Hopf charge\n\\[\nq=2a.\n\\]\nWriting \\(k=2j\\), the charge-\\(q\\) sector occurs at level \\(k\\) iff\n\\[\nk\\ge |q|,\n\\qquad\nk\\equiv q \\pmod 2.\n\\]\nFor fixed \\(q\\) and \\(k\\), the remaining right matrix-coefficient index gives\ndegeneracy \\(k+1\\).\n\\end{lemma}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2707,
      "line_end": 2729,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nBy Peter--Weyl, \\(L^2(S^3)\\cong L^2(SU(2))\\) decomposes into matrix\ncoefficients \\(D^j_{ab}\\), where \\(a,b=-j,-j+1,\\ldots,j\\).  With the\nconvention \\(D^j_{ab}(g)=\\langle a|\\rho_j(g)|b\\rangle\\), left multiplication by\n\\[\nh_\\theta=\\exp(i\\theta\\sigma_3/2),\n\\qquad \\theta\\sim\\theta+4\\pi,\n\\]\ngives\n\\[\nD^j_{ab}(h_\\theta g)=e^{ia\\theta}D^j_{ab}(g).\n\\]\nComparing with Definition~\\ref{p2:def:hopf-charge}, namely\n\\(\\phi(h_\\theta g)=e^{i(q/2)\\theta}\\phi(g)\\), gives \\(q=2a\\).  Since\n\\(a\\) ranges from \\(-j\\) to \\(j\\) in integer steps and \\(k=2j\\), a fixed\ncharge \\(q\\) can occur exactly when\n\\[\nq\\in\\{-k,-k+2,\\ldots,k-2,k\\},\n\\]\nwhich is equivalent to \\(k\\ge |q|\\) and \\(k\\equiv q\\pmod2\\).  Once\n\\(q=2a\\) is fixed, the left index is fixed and the right index \\(b\\) has\n\\(2j+1=k+1\\) possible values.  This gives the stated fixed-charge degeneracy.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "LEMMA",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-024",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "ScalarPeter-WeylcoefficientsD_ab^j witha,b=-j,...,j andthedeclaredleftfibrecharacter."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "Left multiplication of D_ab^j by exp(i theta sigma3/2) gives exp(ia theta), hence q=2a. With k=2j the allowed charges are -k,-k+2,...,k.",
    "This is equivalent to k>=|q| and k congruent to q modulo two. Fixing q fixes a, while b has k+1 values. Summing over all k+1 allowed charges recovers total scalar multiplicity (k+1)^2."
  ],
  "conditions_proposed": [
    "ScalarPeter-Weylsectorandfixedleftaction."
  ],
  "import_labels": [
    "p2:def:hopf-charge",
    "p2:def:finite-diagonal-spin-weight-hopf-charge",

  ],

  "claim_id": "p2:thm:spectrum-by-charge",

  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Spectrum decomposition by integer Hopf charge]\n\\label{p2:thm:spectrum-by-charge}\nThe nonnegative scalar Laplacian $\\Delta_{S^3}$ preserves each integer charge sector $\\mathcal{V}_q$. The spectrum of $\\Delta_{S^3}|_{\\mathcal{V}_q}$ is\n\\begin{equation}\n\\mathrm{Spec}(\\Delta_{S^3}|_{\\mathcal{V}_q}) = \\left\\{ \\frac{k(k+2)}{\\Rmom^2} : k \\geq |q|, \\; k - |q| \\in 2\\ZZ \\right\\},\n\\label{p2:eq:spectrum-charge-n}\n\\end{equation}\nwith degeneracy $(k+1)$ in the fixed charge sector.  Here $k=2j$ is the\nscalar Peter--Weyl level for the diagonal sector $(j,j)$; this statement is\nabout the scalar Laplacian and should not be confused with the full\nnon-diagonal $\\Spin(4)$ module Casimir used for the declared finite package.\n\\end{theorem}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2744,
      "line_end": 2748,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe spectrum, parity restriction, and fixed-charge multiplicity are the\nPaper-I-A scalar Hopf-charge spectrum theorem~\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.\nPaper~II imports it only for kinematic sector classification.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "THEOREM",
  "level": "E1",

{
  "claim_id": "p2:thm:hopf-charge-spectral-gap",

  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",

    "line_end": 2760,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",

  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Exact retained Hopf-charge kinematic spectral gap]\n\\label{p2:thm:hopf-charge-spectral-gap}\nFor Hopf charge $q \\neq 0$, the spectrum of the nonnegative scalar Laplacian $\\Delta_{S^3}|_{\\mathcal{V}_q}$ is bounded below by a strictly positive constant:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\lambda_{\\min}(q) = \\frac{|q|(|q|+2)}{\\Rmom^2} > 0.\n\\label{p2:eq:hopf-charge-spectral-gap}\n\\end{equation}\nEquivalently, the charged sector has a purely kinematic gap in the positive spatial operator.  In a finite scalar-diagonal truncation \\(S^3_m\\), this continuum-sector statement applies only to retained nonempty sectors satisfying \\(|q|\\le m\\) and the charged-mode parity condition \\(k\\equiv |q|\\pmod 2\\).\n\\end{theorem}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2762,
      "line_end": 2766,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nPaper~I-A proves both the geometric lower bound and its associated-line-bundle\nrealization~\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  Imposing the Paper-II retained-sector\ncondition yields the stated kinematic gap.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "THEOREM",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-026",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,

    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Lichnerowicz Formula on $S^3$]\n\\label{p2:thm:lichnerowicz}\nFor any spinor $\\psi$ on the round 3-sphere $S^3(\\Rmom)$,\n\\begin{equation}\nD_{S^3}^{\\,2}\\psi = \\nabla^*\\nabla\\psi + \\frac{\\scal}{4}\\psi = \\nabla^*\\nabla\\psi + \\frac{3}{2\\Rmom^2}\\psi.\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{theorem}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2786,
      "line_end": 2790,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThis is the round-\\(S^3\\) Lichnerowicz identity recorded in\nPaper~I-A~\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  It is repeated here only to state the\nkinematic no-zero consequence.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "THEOREM",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-027",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "UntwistedLevi-CivitaspinDiracoperatoronclosedroundS3(R),scalarcurvature6/R^2."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "The untwisted Levi-Civita spin Lichnerowicz identity is D^2=nabla*nabla+Scal/4. On round S3, Scal=6/R^2, giving the printed 3/(2R^2) term.",
    "The statement uses the smooth spinor core and standard self-adjoint realization. It is not asserted for a generally perturbed or twisted operator merely sharing a principal symbol."
  ],
  "conditions_proposed": [

  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Lichnerowicz no-zero estimate]\n\\label{p2:cor:fermion-gap}\nEvery Dirac eigenvalue $\\lambda$ satisfies\n\\[\n\\lambda^2\\ge \\frac{3}{2\\Rmom^2}.\n\\]\nIn particular, the Lichnerowicz identity rules out harmonic spinors on the positively curved round $S^3$. The sharper exact gap is obtained from the round-sphere spectrum in Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:dirac-spectrum}.\n\\end{corollary}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2801,
      "line_end": 2804,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nFrom Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:lichnerowicz}, $D_{S^3}^{\\,2}=\\nabla^*\\nabla+\\frac{3}{2\\Rmom^2}$.\nSince $\\nabla^*\\nabla$ is non-negative, every Dirac eigenvalue $\\lambda$ satisfies the displayed bound.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "COROLLARY",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-028",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",

  "proof_checks": [

    "This excludes zero, while the sharper absolute gap 3/(2R) is correctly delegated to the exact Dirac spectrum."
  ],

{
  "claim_id": "p2:thm:dirac-spectrum",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0085",
  "source_label": "p2:thm:dirac-spectrum",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 2809,
    "line_end": 2821,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Dirac Spectrum on $S^3$]\n\\label{p2:thm:dirac-spectrum}\nThe Dirac operator $D_{S^3}$ on $S^3(\\Rmom)$ with the unique spin structure has spectrum:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\mathrm{Spec}(D_{S^3}) = \\left\\{ \\pm\\frac{k + 3/2}{\\Rmom} : k = 0, 1, 2, \\ldots \\right\\},\n\\end{equation}\nwith multiplicity $(k+1)(k+2)$ for each individual eigenvalue $+(k+3/2)/\\Rmom$ and $-(k+3/2)/\\Rmom$. Counting both signs together gives $2(k+1)(k+2)$.\n\nThe \\textbf{spinor Dirac spectral gap} is:\n\\begin{equation}\n|{D_{S^3}}|_{\\min} = \\frac{3}{2\\Rmom} = \\frac{3\\Punit}{2\\hbar}.\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{theorem}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2823,
      "line_end": 2828,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe eigenvalues, per-sign multiplicities, and exact first gap are the spinor\npart of the Paper-I-A round-\\(S^3\\) harmonic package\n\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  Paper~II imports this only as a kinematic continuum\nspectrum.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "THEOREM",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-029",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "UniqueS3spinstructure,rounduntwistedspinDirac,importedharmonicpackage, momentumunitPunit=hbar/R."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "The I-A spinor types ((k+1)/2,k/2) and its exchange have eigenvalues +/-(k+3/2)/R. Each individual sign has dimension (k+2)(k+1), and counting both signs doubles it.",
    "The smallest absolute eigenvalue is 3/(2R), with per-sign multiplicity two. Using Punit=hbar/R gives 3Punit/(2hbar) with the correct dimensions.",
    "The theorem imports continuum spinor kinematics, not a physical Hamiltonian or the entire spectrum of a finite module."
  ],
  "conditions_proposed": [
    "RoundLevi-CivitaDiracanddeclaredmomentumunitnormalization."
  ],
  "import_labels": [
    "p1:thm:representation-harmonic-package",
    "p2:subsec:m1-kinematic"
  ],

}

{

  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[No Dirac zero modes]\n\\label{p2:cor:no-dirac-zero}\nOn compact \\(S^3\\) momentum space, there are no zero modes of the Dirac\noperator.  The kinematic Dirac spectrum has the positive operator gap\n\\begin{equation}\n|D_{S^3}|_{\\min}=\\frac{3}{2\\Rmom}.\n\\end{equation}\nThis does not assert the absence of physically massless fields; such an\ninterpretation requires a Hamiltonian, dispersion law, and physical field\nassignment.\n\\end{corollary}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2842,
      "line_end": 2844,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe Dirac spectrum in Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:dirac-spectrum} is $\\pm(k+3/2)/\\Rmom$ with $k\\ge 0$, so $0$ is not an eigenvalue and the smallest absolute eigenvalue is $3/(2\\Rmom)$.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "COROLLARY",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-030",
  "source_replayed": true,

  "premises_consumed": [

  ],

  ],

{
  "claim_id": "UNLABELED:Paper2D:remark:2847",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0087",
  "source_label": null,
  "source": {

    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",

  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{remark}[Lichnerowicz lower bound versus the exact gap]\nOn a closed Riemannian spin manifold \\((M,g)\\), the Lichnerowicz identity\nimplies for every Dirac eigenvalue \\(\\lambda\\) that\n\\[\n\\lambda^2\\ge\\frac14\\min_M\\scal_g.\n\\]\nFor the round \\(S^3(\\Rmom)\\), one has\n\\(\\scal_g=6/\\Rmom^2\\), so\n\\[\n|\\lambda|\\ge\\frac{\\sqrt{3/2}}{\\Rmom}.\n\\]\nThis lower bound proves positivity and excludes zero modes, but it is weaker\nthan the exact first absolute eigenvalue \\(3/(2\\Rmom)\\), which comes from\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:dirac-spectrum}, not from the Lichnerowicz estimate alone.\n\\end{remark}",
  "proof": null,
  "kind": "REMARK",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-E1-031",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "FORMALIZED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "LichnerowiczidentityonaclosedRiemannianspinmanifoldandstandardself-adjointDirac."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "On a closed spin manifold, the gradient norm is nonnegative and the scalar-curvature expectation is at least min(Scal)/4. This yields lambda^2>=min(Scal)/4.",
    "On round S3 the resulting bound is sqrt(3/2)/R, strictly weaker than 3/(2R), since 3/2<9/4 after squaring. Positivity requires positive minimum scalar curvature; the general inequality does not assume every closed spin manifold has it."
  ],

The transverse--traceless spectral\n    sector used below additionally satisfies \\(\\nabla^a h_{ab}=0\\).\n\\end{itemize}\nThus an arbitrary spinor-valued one-form or symmetric two-tensor belongs to\nan ambient reducible bundle and is not, without the displayed projection, a\npure spin-\\(3/2\\) or spin-\\(2\\) field.\n\\end{definition}",

BH-IID-EV-B4-E1-002 — E1

{
  "claim_id": "p2:thm:spin1-spectrum",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0089",
  "source_label": "p2:thm:spin1-spectrum",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 2919,
    "line_end": 2927,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Spectrum of Hodge Laplacian on 1-Forms]\n\\label{p2:thm:spin1-spectrum}\nOn the round 3-sphere $S^3(\\Rmom)$ the Hodge Laplacian $\\Delta_1 = d d^\\dagger + d^\\dagger d$ acting on $1$-forms splits under the Hodge decomposition into exact and coexact parts, with spectra\n\\begin{align}\n\\mathrm{Spec}(\\Delta_1|_{\\mathrm{exact}}) &= \\left\\{ \\frac{k(k+2)}{\\Rmom^2} : k = 1, 2, 3, \\ldots \\right\\},\\\\\n\\mathrm{Spec}(\\Delta_1|_{\\mathrm{coexact}}) &= \\left\\{ \\frac{(k+1)^2}{\\Rmom^2} : k = 1, 2, 3, \\ldots \\right\\}.\n\\end{align}\nThe exact eigenspace at level $k$ has dimension $(k+1)^2$, while the coexact eigenspace at level $k$ has dimension $2k(k+2)$. These are standard vector-harmonic results. \\cite{besse1978manifolds,Camporesi1991}\n\\end{theorem}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2929,
      "line_end": 2945,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nOn $S^3$, the Hodge decomposition for $1$-forms is $\\Omega^1 = d\\Omega^0 \\oplus d^\\dagger\\Omega^2$ since the space of harmonic $1$-forms vanishes ($H^1(S^3)=0$). \n\n\\textbf{Exact branch.}\nLet $f$ be a scalar eigenfunction with $\\Delta_{S^3} f = \\frac{k(k+2)}{\\Rmom^2} f$ and $k\\ge 1$. Then\n\\[\n\\Delta_1(df)=d(\\Delta_{S^3} f)=\\frac{k(k+2)}{\\Rmom^2}\\,df,\n\\]\nso $df$ is an eigen-$1$-form with the same eigenvalue. The scalar eigenspace has dimension $(k+1)^2$. For $k\\ge1$, no nonzero scalar eigenfunction is constant, so $d:E_k\\to\\Omega^1(S^3)$ is injective and $\\dim(dE_k)=(k+1)^2$. Constants occur only in the $k=0$ scalar eigenspace and do not enter the exact branch listed here.\n\n\\textbf{Coexact branch.}\nFor a coexact $1$-form $\\varpi$ with $d^\\dagger\\varpi=0$, in dimension $3$ the coexact branch is conventionally described by the curl operator.  With the self-adjoint curl convention\n\\[\nC:=\\star d\\quad\\text{on coexact one-forms},\n\\]\nup to the harmless sign fixed by the Hodge-star convention one has \\(\\Delta_1\\varpi=C^2\\varpi\\).  The curl spectrum on $S^3(\\Rmom)$ is $\\mathrm{Spec}(C)=\\{\\pm\\frac{k+1}{\\Rmom}:k\\ge 1\\}$, hence the coexact eigenvalues are $\\frac{(k+1)^2}{\\Rmom^2}$. The stated multiplicities are the standard vector-harmonic multiplicities. \\cite{Camporesi1991,besse1978manifolds}\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "THEOREM",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B4-E1-002",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "Untwisted Hodge Laplacian on the round S3; H1(S3)=0; scalar and curl harmonic packages."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "The Hodge decomposition has exact and coexact branches without a harmonic one-form summand. For scalar level k>=1, Delta_1 d=d Delta and d is injective on E_k, giving eigenvalue k(k+2)/R^2 and multiplicity (k+1)^2.",
    "On coexact one-forms, the stated self-adjoint curl has eigenvalues +/- (k+1)/R, k>=1. Squaring gives the positive Hodge eigenvalues. The two chiral representation dimensions sum to 2k(k+2).",
    "The scalar k=0 constant differentiates to zero and is correctly omitted from the exact branch."
  ],

  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Imported retained Levi--Civita square and scalar ground]\n\\label{p2d:thm:canonical-retained-dirac-square}\nPaper~I-A, Corollary~\\ref{p1:cor:canonical-retained-dirac-square}, proves the\nfollowing geometric statement.  Let\n\\(J_R:\\mathcal H_1\\to\\mathcal L_R\\) be the retained smooth realization,\nidentified with the generated carrier by Paper~II-B, and let\n\\[\n \\mathscr D_{\\rm LC}=i(d-d^\\dagger)\\oplus D_{S^3}\n\\]\nbe the canonical Levi--Civita Hodge--de Rham plus spin Dirac representative.\nThen the finite squared compression\n\\[\n K_{\\rm LC}:=J_R^*\\mathscr D_{\\rm LC}^{2}J_R\n\\]\nis diagonal on the retained irreducible sectors, with\n\\[\n\\begin{array}{c|c}\n\\text{retained sector} & K_{\\rm LC}\\\\\n\\hline\n(0,0)\\text{, normalized constant} & 0\\\\\n(\\tfrac12,\\tfrac12)\\text{, exact }dE_1 & 3/\\Rmom^2\\\\\n(1,0)\\oplus(0,1)\\text{, Hodge-dual Killing module}\n & 4/\\Rmom^2\\\\\n(\\tfrac12,0)\\oplus(0,\\tfrac12)\\text{, lowest spinors}\n & 9/(4\\Rmom^2)\n\\end{array}\n\\]\nHence the zero eigenspace of \\(K_{\\rm LC}\\) is exactly the scalar line.\nWrite\n\\[\n \\Pi_{\\rm sc}:=\\mathbf1_{\\{0\\}}(K_{\\rm LC})\n\\]\nfor its spectral projector.  This is a canonical geometric ground projector\ninside the retained smooth realization; it is not by itself a physically\nprepared vacuum state or a physical Hamiltonian ground.\n\\end{theorem}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 2987,
      "line_end": 2993,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",

    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nPaper~I-A derives the four entries from its Hodge and Dirac spectra and proves\nthat the scalar entry is the only zero.  Paper~II-B supplies the\nsame-parent identification of the GP2-generated carrier with that retained\nsmooth model.  The final sentence is a type firewall: neither upstream result\ncontains a physical preparation or Hamiltonian-owner constructor.\n\\end{proof}"

  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[The minimal first-order closure preserves the retained readout]\n\\label{p2d:cor:v215-closure-projected-readout}\nFor any already constituted retained geometric readout\n\\(\\operatorname{Tr}_{15}F(K_{\\rm LC})\\),\nTheorem~\\ref{p1:thm:v215-closure-return} provides the exact expression\n\\[\n \\operatorname{Tr}_{15}F(K_{\\rm LC})\n   =\\operatorname{Tr}_{25}\\bigl(PF(\\widetilde D^2)P\\bigr).\n\\]\nThus the first-order closure can represent that readout without changing\nits retained trace or the specified owner of its square. A coefficient\n\\(1/2\\) would scale the geometric heat-trace difference to\n\\[\n \\frac12\\operatorname{Tr}_{25}e^{-t\\widetilde D^2}\n -\\frac12\\operatorname{Tr}_{15}e^{-tK_{\\rm LC}}\n       =2e^{-3t/R^2}+3e^{-4t/R^2}.\n\\]\nThis is a comparison of the displayed operators. The native III-B\nmomentum action has its actual operator \\(D_p\\); using this particular\nformula in that action additionally requires a certificate identifying\nits actual squared operator and profile with the displayed\n\\(K_{\\rm LC}\\) readout. No such identification follows from the\ncommon carrier, a principal symbol, or the role scalarizer alone.\nThe nonzero difference does not show that the existing action makes\nthat replacement. Likewise,\nthe Schur term \\(L/z\\) is the exact first-order partner return on its\nstated comparison space; interpreting the comparison parameter as a\nphysical clock or populating its ten partner modes requires the actual\noperator, state, and comparison map.\n\\end{corollary}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 3028,
      "line_end": 3033,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"

    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe first equality is the projected functional-calculus identity. The\nsecond follows from the full-trace difference with \\(F(s)=e^{-ts}\\)\nand multiplication by \\(1/2\\). No change of trace is used in\nthe first equality.\n\\end{proof}"

  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[No same-symbol zero-order rigidity]\n\\label{p2d:thm:same-symbol-zero-order-no-go}\nLocality, self-adjointness, \\(\\Spin(4)\\)-equivariance, and the principal symbol\nof \\(\\mathscr D_{\\rm LC}\\) do not determine its square or its ground space.\nIndeed, for every \\(m\\in\\mathbb R\\),\n\\[\n \\mathscr D_m\n :=i(d-d^\\dagger)\\oplus\n   \\left(D_{S^3}+\\frac{m}{\\Rmom}I\\right)\n\\]\nhas the same principal symbol and the same coordinate commutators as\n\\(\\mathscr D_{\\rm LC}\\), while its two lowest spinor-square eigenvalues are\n\\[\n \\frac{(m+3/2)^2}{\\Rmom^2},\\qquad\n \\frac{(m-3/2)^2}{\\Rmom^2}.\n\\]\nAt \\(m=\\pm3/2\\), an additional lowest spin sector reaches zero.  Therefore\nthe spectrum and unique scalar ground of\nTheorem~\\ref{p2d:thm:canonical-retained-dirac-square} are derived only for the\nexplicitly typed canonical Levi--Civita representative, not for the entire\nsame-symbol first-order class.\n\\end{theorem}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 3060,
      "line_end": 3070,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe added term is a local self-adjoint equivariant bundle endomorphism and\ncommutes with every scalar multiplier, so it changes neither the principal\nsymbol nor \\([\\mathscr D_m,M_f]\\).  It shifts the two lowest Dirac\neigenvalues \\(\\pm3/(2\\Rmom)\\) by \\(m/\\Rmom\\).  Squaring gives the displayed\nvalues and the zero modes at \\(m=\\mp3/2\\).  Thus operators satisfying all\nlisted same-symbol hypotheses can have different retained spectra and ground\nmultiplicities.  Paper~II-F, Section~\\ref{p2d:app:form-zero-order-counterfamily} gives a\nsecond counterfamily that also annihilates constants and retains the operator's\nodd grading under exterior-degree parity.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "THEOREM",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B4-E1-005",

    "The phrase \"two lowest spinor-square eigenvalues\" is not literally correct if interpreted as the sorted spectrum of the full displayed smooth operator for every real m. At m=5/2 the k=1 negative Dirac branch reaches zero, whereas the printed original-sector pair is 16/R^2 and 1/R^2. {
  "claim_id": "p2:prop:tt-mode-count",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0095",
  "source_label": "p2:prop:tt-mode-count",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 3119,
    "line_end": 3163,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Exact TT symmetric-tensor mode count]\n\\label{p2:prop:tt-mode-count}\nFor the TT tower of Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:spin2-spectrum}, the multiplicity at level $L\\ge2$ is\n\\begin{equation}\n d_L^{\\mathrm{TT}}=2(L-1)(L+3).\n\\end{equation}\nFor \\(\\lambda\\ge0\\), the exact hard counting function is\n\\begin{equation}\nN_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\lambda)=0\n\\qquad\n\\text{when }\n0\\le\\lambda<\\frac{12}{\\Rmom^2}.\n\\end{equation}\nFor \\(\\lambda\\ge12/\\Rmom^2\\), define\n\\begin{equation}\nM_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\lambda)\n:=\n\\left\\lfloor\\sqrt{\\Rmom^2\\lambda-3}-1\\right\\rfloor,\n\\end{equation}\nso that \\(M_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\lambda)\\ge2\\), and then\n\\begin{equation}\nN_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\lambda)\n=\\sum_{L=2}^{M_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\lambda)}2(L-1)(L+3)\n=\\frac{\nM_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\lambda)\n\\bigl(M_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\lambda)-1\\bigr)\n\\bigl(2M_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\lambda)+11\\bigr)\n}{3}.\n\\end{equation}\nIn particular,\n\\begin{equation}\nN_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\lambda)=\\frac23\\,\\Rmom^3\\lambda^{3/2}+O(\\lambda).\n\\end{equation}\nThus, if the dimensionful Weyl law is written\n\\[\nN_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\lambda)\n=C_{\\mathrm{TT}}\\lambda^{3/2}+O(\\lambda),\n\\]\nthen\n\\[\nC_{\\mathrm{TT}}=\\frac23\\,\\Rmom^3.\n\\]\nEquivalently, after the factor \\(\\Rmom^3\\) is extracted explicitly, the\nremaining dimensionless numerical coefficient is \\(2/3\\).\n\\end{proposition}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 3165,
      "line_end": 3170,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe multiplicity, exact counting function, and Weyl coefficient are\nthe Paper-I-A TT counting result~\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  Paper~II imports\nthose geometric counts and uses them only for finite kinematic occupancy\ncomparisons.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "PROPOSITION",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B4-E1-008",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "Two TT helicity representations ((L+2)/2,(L-2)/2) and its mirror."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "Each branch has dimension (L+3)(L-1), giving total 2(L-1)(L+3). Solving [L(L+2)+4]/R^2<=lambda gives M=floor(sqrt(R^2 lambda-3)-1).",
    "For lambda below 12/R^2 no TT level is retained. Above it, summing the dimensions through M gives M(M-1)(2M+11)/3 exactly.",
    "Since M=R sqrt(lambda)+O(1), the Weyl coefficient is (2/3)R^3, with O(lambda) staircase error. The source correctly distinguishes this dimensionful coefficient from the numerical 2/3."
  ],
  "conditions_proposed": [
    "lambda>=0, with the square-root formula used only above the stated threshold."
  ],
  "import_labels": [

  ],

{
  "claim_id": "p2:cor:finite-tt-scalar-ratio",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0096",
  "source_label": "p2:cor:finite-tt-scalar-ratio",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 3172,
    "line_end": 3193,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Finite tensor/scalar spectral occupancy ratio]\n\\label{p2:cor:finite-tt-scalar-ratio}\nAt the TT level cutoff\n\\[\n\\Lambda_L:=\\frac{L(L+2)+4}{\\Rmom^2},\\qquad L\\ge2,\n\\]\nthe scalar modes are retained through scalar level \\(L\\), while the TT modes\nare retained through TT level \\(L\\).  Let \\(N_0(\\lambda)\\) denote the scalar\nhard counting function and let \\(N_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\lambda)\\) be the hard\ncounting function of Proposition~\\ref{p2:prop:tt-mode-count}.  The finite\ntensor/scalar occupancy ratio at the common spectral cutoff is therefore\n\\begin{equation}\n\\mathcal R_{T/S}(L)\n:=\\frac{N_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\Lambda_L)}{N_0(\\Lambda_L)}\n=\\frac{2L(L-1)(2L+11)}{(L+1)(L+2)(2L+3)}\n=2-\\frac{12(4L+1)}{(L+1)(L+2)(2L+3)}.\n\\end{equation}\nIn particular,\n\\begin{equation}\n\\mathcal R_{T/S}(L)=2-\\frac{24}{L^2}+\\frac{102}{L^3}+O(L^{-4}).\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{corollary}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 3195,
      "line_end": 3205,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nAt the cutoff $\\Lambda_L$, the scalar level $L$ is included because $L(L+2)/\\Rmom^2<\\Lambda_L$, while level $L+1$ is excluded since $(L+1)(L+3)/\\Rmom^2>\\Lambda_L$.  Hence\n\\[\nN_0(\\Lambda_L)=\\sum_{\\ell=0}^L(\\ell+1)^2=\\frac{(L+1)(L+2)(2L+3)}6.\n\\]\nThe TT count through level $L$ is\n\\[\nN_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\Lambda_L)=\\sum_{\\ell=2}^L2(\\ell-1)(\\ell+3)=\\frac{L(L-1)(2L+11)}3.\n\\]\nDividing gives the stated ratio and simplifying against the asymptotic value $2$ gives the finite-cutoff suppression term.  The expansion is the large-$L$ expansion of the displayed rational function.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "COROLLARY",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B4-E1-009",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "Common cutoff Lambda_L=[L(L+2)+4]/R^2, L>=2; exact scalar and TT counts."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "Scalar level L is below that cutoff, while level L+1 exceeds it by (2L-1)/R^2>0. Thus the scalar count is (L+1)(L+2)(2L+3)/6.",
    "Dividing the TT count L(L-1)(2L+11)/3 gives the printed rational ratio and its exact suppression from 2.",
    "The asymptotic expansion is 2-24/L^2+102/L^3+O(L^-4), as direct symbolic expansion confirms. This is finite spectral occupancy, not a dynamical tensor/scalar amplitude ratio."
  ],

  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Lowest TT kinematic gap]\n\\label{p2:cor:lowest-tt-gap}\nThe lowest transverse--traceless tensor harmonics on $S^3(\\Rmom)$ occur at $L=2$ and have eigenvalue\n\\begin{equation}\n\\lambda_{\\min}^{TT}=12/\\Rmom^2.\n\\end{equation}\nThus the TT tensor sector has a strictly positive kinematic gap.     "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThis is immediate from Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:spin2-spectrum}, which gives the TT spectrum and shows that the lowest allowed TT level is $L=2$.\n\\end{proof}"

{
  "claim_id": "p2:thm:spin32-spectrum",
  "audit_id": "BH-IID-C-0098",
  "source_label": "p2:thm:spin32-spectrum",
  "source": {
    "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
    "line_start": 3225,
    "line_end": 3268,
    "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
    "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
  },
  "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
  "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Signed Rarita--Schwinger spectrum on the round $S^3(\\Rmom)$]\n\\label{p2:thm:spin32-spectrum}\nLet $\\slashed{D}_{3/2}$ denote the Rarita--Schwinger operator acting on $\\gamma$-traceless\nspinor-valued $1$-forms on $S^3(\\Rmom)$, i.e.\\ on sections $\\psi$ satisfying\n$\\gamma^i\\psi_i=0$. Then the spectrum splits into two series:\n\\begin{align}\n\\lambda^{(A)}_k &= \\pm \\frac{k+\\tfrac52}{\\Rmom},\n& \\operatorname{mult}_{A,\\pm}(k) &= (k+1)(k+4),\n& k&=0,1,2,\\dots, \\\\\n\\lambda^{(B)}_k &= \\pm \\frac{k+\\tfrac52}{3\\Rmom},\n& \\operatorname{mult}_{B,\\pm}(k) &= (k+2)(k+3),\n& k&=0,1,2,\\dots,\n\\end{align}\nwhere the A-series belongs to \\(\\ker P^*\\), the B-series belongs to\n\\(\\operatorname{Im}P\\), and every displayed multiplicity is a complex\n\\emph{branch multiplicity per sign}.  It is not the total full-operator\nmultiplicity when the two branches share a numerical eigenvalue.  Such\ncollisions occur precisely at\n\\[\n\\lambda^{(A)}_a=\\lambda^{(B)}_{3a+5},\n\\qquad a=0,1,2,\\ldots,\n\\]\nand at those values the complex full-bundle multiplicity per sign is\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\operatorname{mult}_{\\Gamma(S_{3/2})}\n\\!\\left(\\pm\\frac{a+\\tfrac52}{\\Rmom}\\right)\n&=(a+1)(a+4)+(3a+7)(3a+8)\\\\\n&=10(a+2)(a+3).\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\nThe signed spectrum on the smooth round parent is derived independently from its projected Levi--Civita operator in Theorem~\\ref{p2f:thm:v260-signed-rs-s3} of Paper~II-F. It is not a consequence of the finite momentum module. Consequently, the gap on the full \\(\\gamma\\)-traceless vector-spinor bundle is\n\\begin{equation}\n|\\slashed{D}_{3/2}|_{\\min,\\,\\Gamma(S_{3/2})}=\\frac{5}{6\\Rmom}.\n\\end{equation}\nIf one restricts instead to the transverse Rarita--Schwinger summand \\(\\ker P^*\\), the first gap is\n\\begin{equation}\n|\\slashed{D}_{3/2}|_{\\min,\\,\\ker P^*}=\\frac{5}{2\\Rmom}.\n\\end{equation}\nThe sector convention is part of the statement.  The smaller full-bundle\nvalue \\(5/(6\\Rmom)\\) comes from the twistor-image summand; for the transverse\nRarita--Schwinger sector \\(\\ker P^*\\), the first gap is\n\\(5/(2\\Rmom)\\).\n\\end{theorem}",
  "proof": {
    "locator": {
      "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex",
      "line_start": 3270,
      "line_end": 3277,
      "source_corpus": "PapersMinimal-v2_366",
      "source_sha256": "7b1209e4abba4cc3daa394f68ba7d278cd6bcc3bff259afe98503e420c965144"
    },
    "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nTheorem~\\ref{p2f:thm:v260-signed-rs-s3} proves the signed eigenvalues\nand multiplicities by diagonalizing the projected Levi--Civita operator\nin the homogeneous round frame. Proposition~\\ref{p2:prop:rs-spectrum-cross-check}\nindependently identifies the twistor-image and transverse representation\nfamilies. The displayed gap and collision formulas are then finite arithmetic. \nThe earlier imported account remains cited in Paper~I-A and II-F for comparison.\n\\end{proof}"
  },
  "kind": "THEOREM",
  "level": "E1",
  "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B4-E1-011",
  "source_replayed": true,
  "replay_complete_at_stated_scope": true,
  "provisional_status": "REPRODUCED",
  "premises_consumed": [
    "Projected untwisted Levi-Civita gamma-traceless vector-spinor operator on the oriented round parent, with its inherited spin structure."
  ],
  "proof_checks": [
    "The II-F frame proof gives D_(3/2)=(4/(3R))S dot J+5/(2R). The projection coefficient from spin 1/2 onto total fibre spin 3/2 is 1/3, fixing the connection shift without importing the target eigenvalues.",
    "Coupling fibre spin 3/2 to regular spin j gives the four signed branches listed by the source. Reindexing them yields A: +/-(k+5/2)/R, multiplicity (k+1)(k+4), and B: +/-(k+5/2)/(3R), multiplicity (k+2)(k+3).",
    "The independent source representation/twistor argument identifies B with Im(P) and A with ker(P*). The two full-bundle series must both be retained unless the transverse restriction is explicitly imposed.",
    "A/B collisions solve b=3a+5. Adding their per-sign branch dimensions gives 10(a+2)(a+3), as printed. The full-bundle gap is 5/(6R); the transverse-only gap is 5/(2R)."
  ],
  "conditions_proposed": [
