Gauge-related\nprincipal forms are the same unmarked connection realization; the displayed\nrepresentative is not an additional physical selector.         "line_start": 2435,
        "line_end": 2458
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nFor a homogeneous scalar multiple \\(s\\eta_0\\), the principal vertical\nnormalization is\n\\((s\\eta_0)(\\xi_0)=s\\), so it forces \\(s=1\\).  This uniqueness statement is\nonly within the homogeneous scalar-multiple family; it does not exclude\ndistinct gauge-related principal connections such as\n\\(\\eta_0-\\pi^*d\\bar\\chi\\) for a smooth real function\n\\(\\bar\\chi\\) on \\(S^2\\) with \\(d\\bar\\chi\\not\\equiv0\\).\nUsing \\eqref{p2:eq:eta0} and fiber integration directly in the main proof gives\n\\[\n \\int_{S^3}\\eta_0\\wedge d\\eta_0\n =\\int_{S^2}\\!\\left(\\oint_{S^1}\\eta_0\\right)\\omega\n =(2\\pi)(2\\pi)=4\\pi^2,\n\\]\nand hence \\(Q_{\\CS}[\\eta_0]=1\\) in the convention\n\\eqref{p2:eq:cs}.  Applying the character differential\n\\(d\\rho_q:q\\) to the principal connection and curvature gives\n\\(A_q=q\\eta_0-d\\chi\\) and \\(F_q=q\\omega\\); hence\n\\(c_1(L^q)=q[\\omega/(2\\pi)]=q\\).  For\n\\(A_s=s\\eta_0-d\\chi\\), the exact gauge term integrates to zero on closed\n\\(S^3\\), so quadratic scaling gives\n\\(Q_{\\CS}[A_s]=s^2\\).  Applying this with \\(s=q\\) proves the associated-line\nclaim.\n\\end{proof}",

      "from": "p1:prop:contact-normalization",
      "to": "BH-IID-U-prequantum-symplectic-normalization",
      "kind": "IMPORTED_PROOF",
      "branch_id": "BASE_AREA_CURVATURE_NORMALIZATION",
      "scope_guard": "BASE_AREA_CURVATURE_NORMALIZATION",

      "reviewed": true,
      "evidence_function": "SOURCE_PROOF_USE_REVIEW",
      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2517,
        "line_end": 2522
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "We use the Hopf/contact normalization established in Paper~I-A \\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  Thus the Hopf fibration \\(\\Sone \\hookrightarrow S^3 \\xrightarrow{\\pi} S^2\\) realizes $S^3(\\Rmom)$ as a principal $\\mathrm{U}(1)$-bundle over the symplectic manifold $(S^2(\\Rmom/2),\\omega)$. Let $\\vol_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)}$ denote the Riemannian area form, so $\\int_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)}\\vol_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)}=\\pi \\Rmom^2$. We take the normalized symplectic form\n\\[\n\\omega := \\frac{2}{\\Rmom^2}\\,\\vol_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)},\\qquad \\int_{S^2(\\Rmom/2)}\\omega = 2\\pi,\n\\]\nso that the associated complex line bundle $L\\to S^2(\\Rmom/2)$ has $c_1(L)=[\\omega]/(2\\pi)=1$.\n",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0030",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-BH-IID-U-prequantum-symplectic-normalization",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },
    {

      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nPaper~I-A proves this degree-one Boothby--Wang normalization\n\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  The displayed equations translate its physical and\ndimensionless connections into Paper-II notation.\n\\end{proof}",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0031",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-p2:prop:hopf-connection-prequantum-bundle",

    {
      "from": "p1:prop:hopf-scale-dictionary",
      "to": "p2:prop:hopf-connection-prequantum-bundle",
      "kind": "IMPORTED_PROOF",
      "branch_id": "PRINCIPAL_METRIC_SCALE",

        "line_start": 2526,
        "line_end": 2537
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "Let $\\eta_0$ denote the \\emph{dimensionless} principal $\\mathrm{U}(1)$-connection 1-form on the Hopf bundle $S^3\\to S^2$, with principal generator $\\xi_0$ normalized by $\\eta_0(\\xi_0)=1$, and set\n\\[\n\\eta := \\Rmom\\,\\eta_0,\n\\qquad\n\\xi:=\\Rmom^{-1}\\xi_0.\n\\]\nThe metric-scaled contact form is normalized by $\\eta(\\xi)=1$.\nThen the curvature of the principal connection is \\cite{blair2010contact,boyer2008sasakian}\n\\[\nd\\eta_0 = \\pi^* \\omega,\n\\]\nso \\((S^3, \\eta_0)\\) is a prequantum circle bundle over \\((S^2, \\omega)\\) with integer Chern class \\(c_1 = 1\\).",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0032",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-p2:prop:hopf-connection-prequantum-bundle",

        "line_start": 2566,
        "line_end": 2577
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nThe first two identities are the declared principal-to-metric transport.\nSubstitution gives\n\\(\\eta(\\xi)=(\\Rmom\\eta_0)(\\Rmom^{-1}\\xi_0)=1\\), and constancy of\n\\(\\Rmom\\) on the round host gives\n\\(d\\eta=\\Rmom\\,d\\eta_0=\\Rmom\\,\\pi^*\\omega\\).\nOmitting any declared output gives a closure defect once the dictionary is\nlicensed; multiplying either output by an additional free scalar changes the\ngenerated normalization relation.  The remaining quantities occupy distinct\nowner or associated-line slots and therefore are not fixed by this graph.\n\\end{proof}\n",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0033",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-p2d:cor:generated-hopf-normalization-graph",

        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2606,
        "line_end": 2623
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "Let $\\psi\\sim\\psi+4\\pi$ be the standard Hopf fiber angle on\n$S^3\\cong SU(2)$, so that the chosen left-fiber Hopf action is\n\\[\n g\\longmapsto h_\\theta g,\n \\qquad\n h_\\theta:=\\exp(i\\theta\\sigma_3/2),\n \\qquad \\theta\\sim\\theta+4\\pi.\n\\]\nThe Reeb vector field $\\xi = \\frac{2}{\\Rmom}\\partial_\\psi$ generates this fiber action on $S^3(\\Rmom)$. A field $\\phi \\in C^\\infty(S^3)$ has \\textbf{integer Hopf charge} $q \\in \\ZZ$ if\n\\begin{equation}\n\\partial_\\psi \\phi = i\\frac{q}{2}\\,\\phi,\n\\qquad\n\\xi(\\phi)=\\frac{i q}{\\Rmom}\\,\\phi,\n\\qquad\n\\phi(h_\\theta g)=e^{i(q/2)\\theta}\\phi(g).\n\\label{p2:eq:hopf-charge-convention}\n\\end{equation}\nEquivalently, if one uses the $2\\pi$-periodic principal-$U(1)$ parameter $\\alpha=\\theta/2$, the character is $e^{iq\\alpha}$.  The Hilbert space decomposes as $L^2(S^3) = \\bigoplus_{q \\in \\ZZ} \\mathcal{V}_q$, where $\\mathcal{V}_q$ consists of charge-$q$ fields.",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0034",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-p2:def:hopf-charge",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },

        "line_start": 2627,
        "line_end": 2636
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "Charge-$q$ fields are sections of the line bundle $L^q \\to S^2$, where\n$L$ is the degree-one bundle associated to the chosen left-fiber Hopf\nrepresentative. The case $q = 0$ corresponds to functions on the base $S^2$\npulled back to $S^3$; $q \\neq 0$ corresponds to genuinely ``twisted'' fields\nthat cannot be defined on $S^2$ alone.  Throughout this section, $q$ denotes\nthe integer geometric Hopf charge and $q/2$ is the exponent of its\nleft-fiber character in the \\(4\\pi\\) parameter.  This exponent is not\nidentified with the projected Berry label \\(r\\), and both are distinct from\nthe finite diagonal spin weight $\\mathfrak s$ used in the preceding\nfinite-module projector notation.",

      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },

        "line_start": 2679,
        "line_end": 2686
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:time-reversal-action} gives \\(q\\mapsto-q\\).\nThe orbit has one member exactly when \\(q=-q\\) in \\(\\mathbb Z\\), which forces\n\\(q=0\\); its intersection with \\(\\mathbb Z\\setminus\\{0\\}\\) is empty.\nThe parity clause is the left-to-right action proved in\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:parity-action}.     {
      "from": "p2:def:hopf-charge",

      "evidence_function": "SOURCE_PROOF_USE_REVIEW",
      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2708,
        "line_end": 2728
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nBy Peter--Weyl, \\(L^2(S^3)\\cong L^2(SU(2))\\) decomposes into matrix\ncoefficients \\(D^j_{ab}\\), where \\(a,b=-j,-j+1,\\ldots,j\\).  With the\nconvention \\(D^j_{ab}(g)=\\langle a|\\rho_j(g)|b\\rangle\\), left multiplication by\n\\[\nh_\\theta=\\exp(i\\theta\\sigma_3/2),\n\\qquad \\theta\\sim\\theta+4\\pi,\n\\]\ngives\n\\[\nD^j_{ab}(h_\\theta g)=e^{ia\\theta}D^j_{ab}(g).\n\\]\nComparing with Definition~\\ref{p2:def:hopf-charge}, namely\n\\(\\phi(h_\\theta g)=e^{i(q/2)\\theta}\\phi(g)\\), gives \\(q=2a\\).       "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nThis is the round-\\(S^3\\) Lichnerowicz identity recorded in\nPaper~I-A~\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  It is repeated here only to state the\nkinematic no-zero consequence.\n\\end{proof}",

    {

        "line_start": 2802,
        "line_end": 2806
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nFrom Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:lichnerowicz}, $D_{S^3}^{\\,2}=\\nabla^*\\nabla+\\frac{3}{2\\Rmom^2}$.\nSince $\\nabla^*\\nabla$ is non-negative, every Dirac eigenvalue $\\lambda$ satisfies the displayed bound.\n\\end{proof}\n",

      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },

        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2798,
        "line_end": 2799
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\]\nIn particular, the Lichnerowicz identity rules out harmonic spinors on the positively curved round $S^3$. The sharper exact gap is obtained from the round-sphere spectrum in Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:dirac-spectrum}.",

        "line_end": 2829
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nThe eigenvalues, per-sign multiplicities, and exact first gap are the spinor\npart of the Paper-I-A round-\\(S^3\\) harmonic package\n\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.  Paper~II imports this only as a kinematic continuum\nspectrum.\n\\end{proof}",

        "line_start": 2843,
        "line_end": 2845
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nThe Dirac spectrum in Theorem~\\ref{p2:thm:dirac-spectrum} is $\\pm(k+3/2)/\\Rmom$ with $k\\ge 0$, so $0$ is not an eigenvalue and the smallest absolute eigenvalue is $3/(2\\Rmom)$.\n\\end{proof}",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0048",

      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"

    {

      "to": "UNLABELED:Paper2D:remark:2847",
      "kind": "PREMISE_OF",
      "branch_id": "ROUND_BOUND_VS_EXACT",
      "scope_guard": "ROUND_BOUND_VS_EXACT",
      "logic_group": "AND",

      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2849,
        "line_end": 2861
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "On a closed Riemannian spin manifold \\((M,g)\\), the Lichnerowicz identity\nimplies for every Dirac eigenvalue \\(\\lambda\\) that\n\\[\n\\lambda^2\\ge\\frac14\\min_M\\scal_g.\n\\]\nFor the round \\(S^3(\\Rmom)\\), one has\n\\(\\scal_g=6/\\Rmom^2\\), so\n\\[\n|\\lambda|\\ge\\frac{\\sqrt{3/2}}{\\Rmom}.\n\\]\nThis lower bound proves positivity and excludes zero modes, but it is weaker\nthan the exact first absolute eigenvalue \\(3/(2\\Rmom)\\), which comes from\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:dirac-spectrum}, not from the Lichnerowicz estimate alone.",
      "verification_limit": "Claim-matched source use/domain inspection, not an independent audit of untargeted manuscripts.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B3-EDGE-0049",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B3-ROUTE-UNLABELED:Paper2D:remark:2847",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B3-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },

        "line_start": 7265,
        "line_end": 7272
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "The diagonal-weight table above gives\n\\[\n\\dim_\\CC \\mathcal H_1^{(-1/2)}=\\dim_\\CC \\mathcal H_1^{(+1/2)}=2.\n\\]\nThe preceding proposition shows that the Fourier-averaging projectors onto \\(\\mathfrak s=\\pm\\tfrac12\\) isolate exactly those two sectors. Although the projector formula uses a chosen Cartan axis, the resulting direct sum is the invariant spinor submodule \\(V_{1/2,0}\\oplus V_{0,1/2}\\) inside \\(\\mathcal H_1\\).\n\\end{proof}\n\nThe diagonal-weight grading therefore isolates the protected eight-real-dimensional spinor module as a canonical-relative kinematic block.       "to": "p2:thm:spin1-spectrum",
      "kind": "IMPORTED_PROOF",
      "branch_id": "COEXACT_ONE_FORMS",

      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 2930,
        "line_end": 2946
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nOn $S^3$, the Hodge decomposition for $1$-forms is $\\Omega^1 = d\\Omega^0 \\oplus d^\\dagger\\Omega^2$ since the space of harmonic $1$-forms vanishes ($H^1(S^3)=0$). \n\n\\textbf{Exact branch.}\nLet $f$ be a scalar eigenfunction with $\\Delta_{S^3} f = \\frac{k(k+2)}{\\Rmom^2} f$ and $k\\ge 1$. Then\n\\[\n\\Delta_1(df)=d(\\Delta_{S^3} f)=\\frac{k(k+2)}{\\Rmom^2}\\,df,\n\\]\nso $df$ is an eigen-$1$-form with the same eigenvalue. The scalar eigenspace has dimension $(k+1)^2$. For $k\\ge1$, no nonzero scalar eigenfunction is constant, so $d:E_k\\to\\Omega^1(S^3)$ is injective and $\\dim(dE_k)=(k+1)^2$. Constants occur only in the $k=0$ scalar eigenspace and do not enter the exact branch listed here.\n\n\\textbf{Coexact branch.}\nFor a coexact $1$-form $\\varpi$ with $d^\\dagger\\varpi=0$, in dimension $3$ the coexact branch is conventionally described by the curl operator.  With the self-adjoint curl convention\n\\[\nC:=\\star d\\quad\\text{on coexact one-forms},\n\\]\nup to the harmless sign fixed by the Hodge-star convention one has \\(\\Delta_1\\varpi=C^2\\varpi\\).  The curl spectrum on $S^3(\\Rmom)$ is $\\mathrm{Spec}(C)=\\{\\pm\\frac{k+1}{\\Rmom}:k\\ge 1\\}$, hence the coexact eigenvalues are $\\frac{(k+1)^2}{\\Rmom^2}$. The stated multiplicities are the standard vector-harmonic multiplicities. \\cite{Camporesi1991,besse1978manifolds}\n\\end{proof}",
      "verification_limit": "Source-use/type mapping only; E1/E3/E4 reviewers own correctness adjudication.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B4-EDGE-0001",
      "proof_route_id": "BH-IID-B4-ROUTE-p2:thm:spin1-spectrum",
      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B4-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },

        "line_end": 3210
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nAt the cutoff $\\Lambda_L$, the scalar level $L$ is included because $L(L+2)/\\Rmom^2<\\Lambda_L$, while level $L+1$ is excluded since $(L+1)(L+3)/\\Rmom^2>\\Lambda_L$.  Hence\n\\[\nN_0(\\Lambda_L)=\\sum_{\\ell=0}^L(\\ell+1)^2=\\frac{(L+1)(L+2)(2L+3)}6.\n\\]\nThe TT count through level $L$ is\n\\[\nN_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\Lambda_L)=\\sum_{\\ell=2}^L2(\\ell-1)(\\ell+3)=\\frac{L(L-1)(2L+11)}3.\n\\]\nDividing gives the stated ratio and simplifying against the asymptotic value $2$ gives the finite-cutoff suppression term.  The expansion is the large-$L$ expansion of the displayed rational function.\n\\end{proof}",

        "line_start": 3200,
        "line_end": 3210
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nAt the cutoff $\\Lambda_L$, the scalar level $L$ is included because $L(L+2)/\\Rmom^2<\\Lambda_L$, while level $L+1$ is excluded since $(L+1)(L+3)/\\Rmom^2>\\Lambda_L$.  Hence\n\\[\nN_0(\\Lambda_L)=\\sum_{\\ell=0}^L(\\ell+1)^2=\\frac{(L+1)(L+2)(2L+3)}6.\n\\]\nThe TT count through level $L$ is\n\\[\nN_{\\mathrm{TT}}(\\Lambda_L)=\\sum_{\\ell=2}^L2(\\ell-1)(\\ell+3)=\\frac{L(L-1)(2L+11)}3.\n\\]\nDividing gives the stated ratio and simplifying against the asymptotic value $2$ gives the finite-cutoff suppression term.  The expansion is the large-$L$ expansion of the displayed rational function.\n\\end{proof}",
      "verification_limit": "Source-use/type mapping only; E1/E3/E4 reviewers own correctness adjudication.",
      "note": "Only exact scalar count polynomial, not Weyl approximation, is used for finite ratio.",

      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B4-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },

        "line_start": 3302,
        "line_end": 3326
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "On the fixed full momentum carrier \\(\\mathcal H_p=\\mathcal H_1\\),\nuse the primitive left generator \\(Q_H:=Q_{H,L}=-2L_3^-\\).\nThen\n\\[\n \\mathcal H_1|_{U(1)_H}\n =7\\chi_0\\oplus3\\chi_1\\oplus3\\chi_{-1}\\oplus\\chi_2\\oplus\\chi_{-2},\n \\qquad Q_H(Q_H^2-I)(Q_H^2-4I)=0.\n\\]\nIts multiplicities at \\(q=-2,-1,0,1,2\\) are \\(1,3,7,3,1\\).\nIn this left convention the extreme weights \\(q=\\pm2\\) occur in\n\\(V_{0,1}\\); for the geometric right convention they occur in \\(V_{1,0}\\).\nThey are absent from the scalar harmonic submodule \\(E_0\\oplus E_1\\).\n\\end{proposition}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nOn \\(V_{j_L,j_R}\\), the charge is \\(-2m_R\\) with multiplicity \\(2j_L+1\\).\nThe six summands contribute, in the order\n\\((0,0),(\\tfrac12,0),(0,\\tfrac12),\n(\\tfrac12,\\tfrac12),(1,0),(0,1)\\),\n\\[\n \\chi_0,\\quad 2\\chi_0,\\quad\n \\chi_{-1}+\\chi_1,\\quad 2\\chi_{-1}+2\\chi_1,\\quad\n 3\\chi_0,\\quad \\chi_{-2}+\\chi_0+\\chi_2.\n\\]\nSumming gives the stated character and hence the polynomial identity.",

    {

        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 3373,
        "line_end": 3392
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "For\n$\\mathcal P_x(m_x)=\\bigoplus_{k=0}^{m_x}E_k^x$ with\n$E_k^x\\cong V_{k/2}\\otimes V_{k/2}^*$, degree $k$ has weights\n$-k,-k+2,\\ldots,k$, each with multiplicity $k+1$.  Hence\n\\[\n \\operatorname{spec}(Q_H|_{\\mathcal P_x(m_x)})=\\{-m_x,\\ldots,m_x\\}.\n\\]\nFor $|q|\\le m_x$, writing\n$r=\\lfloor(m_x-|q|)/2\\rfloor$, the exact multiplicity is\n\\[\n d_{m_x}(q)=(r+1)(|q|+1+r),\n\\]\nand\n\\[\n D_{m_x}:=\\dim\\mathcal P_x(m_x)\n =\\frac{(m_x+1)(m_x+2)(2m_x+3)}6.\n\\]\nThus $m_p=1$ does not impose a universal bound on later position-clock\nweights.\n\\end{proposition}",

      "kind": "IMPORTED_PROOF",

      "evidence_function": "SOURCE_PROOF_USE_REVIEW",
      "source_use_locator": {
        "file": "Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_134.tex",
        "line_start": 3402,
        "line_end": 3432
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "Use the left-action convention of\nCorollary~\\ref{p2d:cor:hopf-rotation-transvection}, and set\n\\[\n Q_i:=Q_{H,L,i}^{x}=-2L_{i,x}^-.\n\\]\nFor the nonnegative scalar Laplacian restricted to this band,\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\sum_{i=1}^{3}Q_i^2=a^2\\Delta_a.}\n\\]\nFor every spectral weight \\(W=w(\\Delta_a)\\) on the band,\n\\[\n \\operatorname{Tr}(WQ_iQ_j)\n =\\frac{a^2\\delta_{ij}}{3}\\operatorname{Tr}(W\\Delta_a).\n\\]\nThe same identities hold for the explicitly chosen right chiral triple\n\\(Q_i=2L_{i,x}^+\\).  They concern complete scalar bands and chiral\ngenerators; no clock-energy calibration or Hamiltonian premise is used.\n\\end{corollary}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nOn \\(E_k^x\\), the chosen chiral factor has spin \\(j=k/2\\), so\n\\[\n \\sum_iQ_i^2=4j(j+1)I=k(k+2)I=a^2\\Delta_a|_{E_k^x}.\n\\]\nThe complete band is invariant under the chiral action, so the finite direct\nsum proves the operator identity without a compression defect.\nThe weight \\(W\\) commutes with that action; hence\n\\(T_{ij}:=\\operatorname{Tr}(WQ_iQ_j)\\) is an invariant two-tensor for\nthe adjoint \\(SO(3)\\) action and equals \\(c\\delta_{ij}\\).\nSumming its diagonal entries gives\n\\(3c=a^2\\operatorname{Tr}(W\\Delta_a)\\).",
      "verification_limit": "Source-use/type mapping only; E1/E3/E4 reviewers own correctness adjudication.",
      "id": "BH-IID-B4-EDGE-0027",

      "evidence_id": "BH-IID-EV-B4-SOURCE-MAPPING"
    },

        "line_end": 3500
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "\\begin{proof}\nCorollary~\\ref{p2d:cor:hopf-rotation-transvection} identifies the\nleft-action operator with $-i\\mathcal V_i^L$; rescaling radius gives\n$D_i=(\\hbar/a)Q_i$. A Killing field commutes with the round scalar\nLaplacian, hence $D_i$ preserves each $E_k^x$, establishing the exact\nrestriction and its chiral Casimir square. The ordinary parent\nfirst-order symbol of $D_i$ is $\\hbar\\xi(e_i)=p(e_i)$; frame\northonormality gives the quadratic symbol identity. Restricting the\nfinite square to $E_k^x$ yields\n$\\hbar^2k(k+2)/a^2$.\nThe finite-rank extension has a smooth kernel (the finite band is a sum\nof smooth eigenspaces), and is therefore smoothing. Its intrinsic\norder-one symbol is zero, proving the necessity of the inherited label.\n\\end{proof}",

      "source_use_excerpt": "A parity-preserving completely positive \\emph{map} of the even\nobservable algebra can mix its central populations; this does not\nmake its possible odd Kraus operators accessible as field effects.\nThe conditional transfer generator in\nTheorem~\\ref{p4a:thm:v352-two-rate-transfer} explicitly shows the\ndifference.         "line_start": 3909,
        "line_end": 3932
      },
      "source_use_excerpt": "On the regular local metric-$f_c(R)$ cap chart of\nTheorem~\\ref{p3f:thm:v223-cap-parent}, put $\\Phi=f_c'(r)$ and\n$\\chi=f_c''(r)>0$. Corollary~\\ref{p3f:cor:v260-canonical-exchange}\nproves the exact canonical exchange, with a \\emph{constant} $\\eta\\ne0$,\n\\[\n P_c=\\eta r,\\qquad Q=-\\chi(r)p_\\Phi/\\eta,\\qquad\n p_\\Phi\\,d\\Phi=P_c\\,dQ-d(P_cQ).\n\\]\nThe notation $P_c$ distinguishes this momentum coordinate from the\nEinstein coefficient $P_E$ of the capped density. The phase action\nretains the $-[P_cQ]$ endpoint change, the full pulled-back Hamiltonian\nand all source/boundary terms of its actual owner; the resulting\nquadratic term contains $Q^2/\\chi^2$ and a $p_aQ$ cross term rather\nthan an unchanged $P_c^2$ flux.\nProposition~\\ref{p3f:prop:v260-jordan-flux} derives the Jordan lapse\nconstraint and canonical boundary momentum from that same restricted\naction and exhibits on-shell slices of equal curvature and induced\nmetric with opposite scalar momenta. Corollary~\n\\ref{p3f:cor:v260-conormal-jordan-distinction} evaluates the distinct\nconormal source norm and its necessary/sufficient amplitude match.\nNeither the coordinate exchange nor a fixed curvature profile proves\na physical incoming conormal amplitude or the occurrence of the cap\nin the full common action; those identifications keep their explicit\nIII-E/III-F source-owner obligations.",
      "verification_limit": "Source-use/type mapping only; E1/E3/E4 reviewers own correctness adjudication.",

Independent verification certificates — Paper II-D batch 1

Input: Sources-v2_366/Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex, lines 1–1016, source corpus v2.366. Reviewer: /root/independent_checks. No inherited audit verdict or other agent's proposal was consulted before these provisional certificates. These arguments verify existing propositions only. They do not establish occurrence, a Hamiltonian, a dispersion identification, or global physical realization.

<a id="HEAT-001"></a>

BH-IID-EV-E3-HEAT-001 — finite semigroup

A commuting family of finite-dimensional self-adjoint operators is simultaneously diagonalizable. The semigroup law makes the family commute. In a joint eigenline its eigenvalue is a continuous multiplicative function v(t) in [0,1] with v(0)=1. It cannot vanish: for any t choose n sufficiently large that v(t/n)>0, and v(t)=v(t/n)^n. Thus log v(t) is continuous and additive on nonnegative reals. It is -lambda*t, lambda>=0. The stated derivative at zero identifies these lambda with the eigenvalues of L. Consequently V_t=exp(-tL). This uses scalar Cauchy functional equations, rather than the source matrix ODE argument. The proof covers degeneracy, a zero generator, and the zero-dimensional space.

For the specified closure, use the canonical identification H* tensor H = End(H). Its coevaluation corresponds to the identity; pairing after applying T is the matrix pairing with that identity, sum_i T_ii. Spectral projectors P_lambda therefore contribute rank(P_lambda)*exp(-t lambda). This verifies the canonical closure value and dimensional block coefficients; the occurrence equality is an explicit separate antecedent, not a derived physical action claim.

<a id="SPECTRAL-002"></a>

BH-IID-EV-E3-SPECTRAL-002 — finite counts and readouts

SU(2) spin j has dimension 2j+1, so the two-factor block has the product dimension. The chosen symmetric Casimir is by definition 2(C_L+C_R)/R^2. On diagonal j_L=j_R=k/2 it is k(k+2)/R^2, while the full package includes nondiagonal modules; these are never treated as scalar functions on S3. The triangular full-package count is sum_{a+b<=2m}(a+1)(b+1)=binomial(2m+4,4), using the coefficient generating function (1-z)^(-5). The scalar count is sum_{k=0}^m(k+1)^2=(m+1)(m+2)(2m+3)/6. At m=1 the full block data from exact rational enumeration are dimension 15, eigenvalues times R^2 equal to 0, 3/2, 3/2, 4, 4, 3 with multiplicities 1,2,2,3,3,4; scalar dimension is 5. The finite spectral traces in the source follow by the trace of each block. The sole zero Casimir is (0,0), excluded in the zeta sum. Every retained positive lambda contributes exp(-s log lambda), entire in complex s; finite sums remain entire, including the empty m=0 positive spectrum (zero function).

For scalar parent counting put N=floor(sqrt(1+R^2 lambda)) for lambda>=0. The exact count is sum_{n=1}^N n^2. Since N=R sqrt(lambda)+O(1), this is R^3 lambda^(3/2)/3+O(lambda). This independently checks the table's Weyl term. Resolvent poles, strict positivity for logarithms, and zero-mode exclusions are required exactly as stated in the source process table.

<a id="COUPLING-010"></a>

BH-IID-EV-E3-COUPLING-010 — fixed typed equivariant coupling

Amendment requested during integration: the typed-coupling record has its own argument rather than relying on the finite-dimension/Casimir certificate. For G=SU(2)L times SU(2)_R, write an irreducible mode space as U(a,b)=V_a tensor V_b. For two fixed source types and one fixed target type, the universal tensor-product property and the direct-product action give Hom_G(U_(a,b) tensor U_(c,d), U_(e,f)) canonically isomorphic to Hom_SU(2)(V_a tensor V_c,V_e) tensor Hom_SU(2)(V_b tensor V_d,V_f). Each SU(2) tensor product is multiplicity free: V_e occurs exactly when |a-c|<=e<=a+c with a+c-e an integer, and similarly |b-d|<=f<=b+d with b+d-f an integer. Otherwise the corresponding Hom space is zero. Thus both factors impose selection rules independently. Once bases and a specific pointwise bundle contraction are fixed, the coefficients of that contraction projected to target modes are coordinates of these Hom maps, hence left and right Clebsch–Gordan coefficients times the contraction's reduced coefficient(s). For successive couplings, expressing the same map in different parenthesized tensor decompositions is exactly recoupling. Bundle multiplicity/embedding data and the chosen contraction supply any additional reduced coefficients; the statement does not assert that they are fixed by representation labels alone. With the target or contraction unspecified, there is no particular Hom map and hence no universal coupling coefficient. This basis-free direct-product Hom argument checks the existing source remark's limited, explicitly typed assertion, not a new physical coupling law.

<a id="POISSON-003"></a>

BH-IID-EV-E3-POISSON-003 — parent heat asymptotics

Put u=t/R^2. The shifted spectrum gives Z(t)=exp(u)sum_{n>=1} n^2 exp(-u n^2). Poisson summation of a Gaussian gives Theta(u)=sum_{n in Z}exp(-u n^2)=sqrt(pi/u)sum_{ell in Z}exp(-pi^2 ell^2/u). Differentiation is justified by absolute uniform convergence on compact positive u intervals. Then Z(t)=exp(u)sqrt(pi)/(4u^(3/2)) [1+2 sum_{ell>=1}(1-2pi^2 ell^2/u)exp(-pi^2 ell^2/u)]. The bracket differs from 1 by an exponentially small quantity as u decreases to zero. Expanding exp(u) gives exactly 1+u+u^2/2+O(u^3). The leading factor sqrt(pi)R^3/4 equals Vol(S3(R))/(4pi)^(3/2). This is an independent spectral/theta-function certificate, not the source curvature invariant substitution. It applies to the positive radius, positive small-time parent; no finite fixed carrier has this singular short-time expansion.

<a id="ZETA-004"></a>

BH-IID-EV-E3-ZETA-004 — direct Dirichlet continuation

For Re(s)>3/2 the shifted source series is absolutely convergent. Binomial expansion and absolutely convergent rearrangement give zeta_Delta(s)=R^(2s)sum_{j>=0}(s)_j/j! *[zeta_R(2s+2j-2)-1]. Here (s)_j is the rising factorial and zeta_R the Riemann zeta function. On a compact s set, the large-j bracket decays exponentially (bounded by a constant times 4^(-j)), and (s)_j/j! grows at most polynomially. Hence this sum converges normally away from its isolated poles and supplies the continuation to every compact subset of C. For j>=0, the only corresponding pole is s_j=3/2-j, with residue R^(3-2j)(s_j)_j/(2j!). All these half-integer residues are nonzero for this round spectrum. The leading residue is R^3/2, equal to Vol/(4pi)^(3/2)/Gamma(3/2). Thus the source's possible-poles theorem holds (and its displayed S3 pole list is correct). This route is independent of source heat-Mellin continuation. The accompanying script checks the first seven residues exactly against heat coefficients; the normal-convergence argument proves the all-j statement.

<a id="COMPRESSION-005"></a>

BH-IID-EV-E3-COMPRESSION-005 — fixed bands and readouts

Let i_K and i_m be isometric inclusions of B_K and H_m into the parent Hilbert space. Nestedness gives i_m J=i_K. Therefore J* i_m* O i_m J = i_K* O i_K for every operator whose stated domain contains H_m. This identity is exact for arbitrary O, with all maps defined on the finite input band. For a spectral F(Delta), each E_k is invariant and the restriction is diagonal, so the compressed operator is also the genuine restricted operator and every F value is unchanged. This distinguishes generic double compression from an invariant restriction.

Applying the same finite scalar functional to equal operators gives equal values. For a trace this is trace equality; for fixed boundary data it is the same matrix coefficient. Neither statement compares a trace on all H_m to a trace on B_K, nor generates a performed readout. This separately checks the source's process-readout corollary.

Given upstream m_p=1, the admissible scalar momentum bands are K<=1. No large-m_p argument is involved. On a position frontier F containing B_K, its orthogonal projection acts identically on that band. Complete-band frontiers F=P_x(m_x) satisfy B_K subset F iff m_x>=K because all harmonic shells are nonzero and mutually orthogonal. Physical frontier occurrence, continued stage occurrence and momentum persistence remain the exact upstream conditional/established inputs respectively.

<a id="WORD-006"></a>

BH-IID-EV-E3-WORD-006 — guard bands

Restricted ambient polynomials of total degree <=r span P_x(r). Their product filtration is immediate from total degree, without invoking a finite compressed multiplication identity. The intermediate vector after j symbols has degree <=K+sum_{a<=j}s_a. Under m>=K+sum_all s_a each intermediate projection is the identity. Induction proves equality of the entire word to parent multiplication as vectors, hence zero norm remainder on the declared input band. This holds for zero degree symbols, empty words, and exact guard equality. It does not imply equality without that buffer. The conditional stage rule F_0=P_x(1), F_{n+1}=span(F_n,E_1 F_n) gives F_n=P_x(n+1) by polynomial degree decomposition, so substitution yields the stated n+1 guard certificate. This verifies the existing stagewise import within its admitted-rule antecedent and does not assert the rule occurs.

<a id="KERNEL-007"></a>

BH-IID-EV-E3-KERNEL-007 — Berezin symbol error

Use the orthonormal Chebyshev basis U_j for the S3 zonal semicircle measure (2/pi)*sqrt(1-s^2) ds. For C_m(s)=sum_{j=0}^m (j+1)U_j(s), Parseval gives integral C_m^2=d_m. The three-term recurrence s U_j=(U_{j+1}+U_{j-1})/2, U_-1=0, gives integral s C_m^2=sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(j+1)(j+2). Thus the normalized kernel has integral s equal to 2m/(2m+3). Chord squared on the unit sphere is 2(1-s), yielding exactly 6/(2m+3). This differs from the source tensor-product/character coefficient derivation.

Positivity and Jensen/Cauchy-Schwarz give |B_m f(q)-f(q)|<=L_fE[physical chord]<=L_fR*sqrt(6/(2m+3)). Solving the squared inequality and taking the least nonnegative integer gives exactly the printed ceiling bound. This includes m=0 and L_f=0. Tensoring with a fixed identity is isometric in operator norm, so position-only tests acquire no momentum error term; a genuinely two-factor symbol has a separate fixed momentum concentration term, not an unproved vanishing limit.

<a id="BOUNDARY-008"></a>

BH-IID-EV-E3-BOUNDARY-008 — cutoff topology and operator identities

The source's scalar boundary claims can also be checked by a moment/kernel route. The radius defect D=I-sum C_a^2 is supported only on E_m: multiplication can leave the band only from that shell, and D=sum P M_a(1-P)M_a P. SO(4) equivariance makes D a scalar on irreducible E_m. Independently, Tr(sum C_a^2)=integral integral (x dot y)|C_m(x dot y)|^2 dσ(x)dσ(y) =d_m2m/(2m+3), by the recurrence calculation above. Hence Tr(D)=3d_m/(2m+3)=(m+1)(m+2)/2. Divide by dim(E_m)=(m+1)^2 to obtain D=(m+2)/(2(m+1))Q_m, including m=0.

For the commutator, its support is also E_m. The O(4)-equivariant map from bivectors into End(E_m) is a scalar multiple of rotation L_ab: SO(4) has one copy each of the two adjoint types here and orientation reversal equates coefficients. Take h=(x_a+i x_b)^m, m>=1. The complex raising coordinate z=x_a+i x_b sends h entirely to E_{m+1}, so C_z h=0. The projection of bar(z)h to E_{m-1} is alphaz^(m-1). Since |z|^2 has the uniform [0,1] law on S3, its beta moments give alpha=(1/(m+1))/(1/m)=m/(m+1). Then ||C_bar(z)h||^2/||h||^2=m/(m+1). From [C_bar(z),C_z]=2i[C_a,C_b] and L_ab h=im*h, the common coefficient is 1/(2(m+1)). At m=0 both sides vanish. Thus the printed commutator has the correct coefficient and sign. Rotation weights range from -m to m, attaining m on h, giving norm m/(2(m+1)). Radius norm tends to 1/2, as does the commutator norm. Since Q_m annihilates every fixed finite band eventually and both families are uniformly bounded, the defects converge strongly to zero. The normalized radius trace is exactly 3/(2m+3).

The script independently builds coordinate compression matrices from an ambient polynomial quotient and exact S3 moments at m=0,1,2,3. It verifies all six commutators and radius formulas, supplying checkable controls independent of a harmonic raising/lowering implementation.

For general well-defined compositions insert I=P+Q into PABP: PABP=PAPBP+PAQBP. This proves the product defect. When D commutes with P, [PDP,PM_fP]=P[D,M_f]P=P M_{Df}P, by the Leibniz rule. The finite smooth band supplies the operator-domain core. These formulas do not make a whole-carrier norm convergence claim.

<a id="FLAT-009"></a>

BH-IID-EV-E3-FLAT-009 — extrinsic exponential chart

Embed S3(R) in R4 and take p=(0,0,0,R). The exponential is exp_p(v)=(R sin(r/R) v/r, R cos(r/R)), r=|v|. Differentiate directly. A unit radial variation has derivative of Euclidean norm one. A tangential variation perpendicular to v has derivative multiplied by R sin(r/R)/r. Cross terms vanish. The pullback metric therefore has radial eigenvalue 1 and two tangential eigenvalues sinc(r/R)^2, without using the source polar-coordinate metric formula.

On 0<rho<pi, d(sin rho/rho)/d rho has numerator rho cos rho-sin rho. Its derivative is -rho sin rho<0 and it starts at zero. Thus sinc^2 decreases strictly to zero and the displayed L-dependent lower bound is sharp as a supremum approached as r increases to L on the open ball. For 0<=rho<=1, sin rho/rho>=1-rho^2/6>=0 implies 1-sinc(rho)^2<=rho^2/3-rho^4/36<=rho^2/3. No C^1, operator or dynamics estimate is implied. The flatness predicate is therefore an explicit ratio check on the exact round branch, with no new independent geometry assumption.

Independent verification — Paper II-D batch 2

Reviewer: /root/independent_checks. Target: current v2.366 corpus, Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_132.tex, lines 1017–2060. The provisional assessment was recorded before receiving other reviewers' findings. No batch2 replay, mapper or adversarial proposal was read. A subsequent coordinator message identified the literal isotropy-group phrase at line 1357; certificate TYPE-011 checks that phrase independently below. All other certificates use exact source claims, definitions and narrowed current-source imports. No paper was modified and no new framework theorem or repair was developed.

<a id="CHIRAL-001"></a>

BH-IID-EV-B2-E3-CHIRAL-001

Identify so(4) with bivectors in oriented Euclidean four-space. The Hodge star has square one on bivectors and its positive and negative eigenspaces have dimension three each. The Hodge star commutes with the orientation-preserving SO4 adjoint action; differentiation gives [X,Y]=[X,Y], so its two eigenspaces are ideals. A cross-ideal bracket belongs to both eigenspaces and therefore vanishes. The induced metric is negative definite on compact rotation generators. Thus the two ideals are the compact real su(2) factors. Writing spatial rotations and transvections in their self-dual/anti-self-dual combinations gives exactly L+ = (J+RP)/(2 hbar), L-=(J-RP)/(2 hbar). This identifies the source's linear combinations by geometric self-duality, rather than deriving the direct sum solely by its printed bracket expansion. The inverse relations follow from adding/subtracting the two self-dual projections. The construction needs R>0 and nonzero normalization hbar, which are the declared kinematic normalization domains. It splits Killing symmetry algebra, not the underlying single S3 carrier into two parents.

<a id="CENTER-002"></a>

BH-IID-EV-B2-E3-CENTER-002

Realize spin j as Sym^(2j)(C2). The central -I acts as (-1)^(2j); hence the diagonal Spin(4) center acts on type (jL,jR) by (-1)^(2(jL+jR)). This constructively proves the descent criterion: a representation factors through the quotient exactly when that kernel is trivial on it. The protected (1/2,0) and (0,1/2) sectors therefore fail SO4 descent, while the coordinate (1/2,1/2) type descends. This is a representation lift of one geometric parent, not a new geometric parent.

At level one the central character is +1 on dimensions 1,4,3,3 and -1 on dimensions 2,2. Thus H+ has dimension11, H- dimension4 and Tr Gamma=7. Since Gamma is a represented involutive unitary, Gamma*=Gamma=Gamma^-1, and its spectral projectors are (1±Gamma)/2. The adjoint action of Gamma on End(H) has character (Tr Gamma)^2=49 and total dimension225, so its ± eigenspace dimensions are (225±49)/2=137,88. This character computation independently checks the source rectangular-block count; the eigenspaces are the respective same-character and opposite-character Hom summands.

An equivariant vector map X:V_coord tensor H -> H must intertwine the center. Since zc acts trivially on V_coord, its input/output H characters agree, so X is central even. Rotation/transvection generators commute with all central group elements, as do equivariant projectors. The commutant of Gamma is a unital star algebra and is closed under finite functional calculus, proving the inclusion for every word actually licensed by this kinematic grammar. It does not assert all ambient End(H) operations are physically generated. For an invariant central-odd bridge, Hom_G(H-,H+)=0 and Hom_G(H+,H-)=0: the irreducible sector supports are disjoint. Hence its odd component must vanish by complete reducibility. This is an alternative intertwiner-support proof of the existing no-bridge lemma.

On one irreducible sector, central conjugation is trivial even for a spinorial representation. On a direct sum it is trivial precisely on same-character blocks; opposite-character maps are not claimed to descend. This certifies the operator-level descent scope in the source remark.

<a id="ANTIPODAL-HOPF-003"></a>

BH-IID-EV-B2-E3-ANTIPODAL-HOPF-003

For g in SU2, quaternion multiplication gives (-I,I):g -> -g, (I,-I):g -> -g and (-I,-I):g -> g. The kernel of the Spin4 action consists exactly of (I,I),(-I,-I): if agb^-1=g for all g, then a=b and a commutes with every SU2 matrix, hence a=b=±I. Thus the antipodal isometry has exactly these two specified lifts, which differ by the diagonal kernel. On scalar degree-k harmonic polynomials antipodal parity is (-1)^k, while zc is +1 on every scalar harmonic. Independent E3 review of the two Paper II-D corrections

Source: Paper2D-SymmetrySpectra-v2_133.tex in the supplied update working corpus v2.367. Reviewer: /root/independent_checks. Scope is exactly the two corrected source objects and their actual proof statements; no other new source claim was audited or edited in this review.

BH-IID-EV-UPDATE-E3-G002

The new proof explicitly keeps K=SU(2)_diag and states that its action on the tangent module p factors through K/{±I}=SO(3). This is correct: p is the anti-diagonal tangent module {(A,-A):A in su(2)}. A diagonal (u,u) sends it to (Ad_u A,-Ad_u A). The adjoint kernel consists exactly of u=±I, while conjugation by unit quaternions rotates all imaginary quaternions. Thus the effective quotient is SO(3); K itself has not been identified with that quotient.

To verify the theorem independently, write a scalar order-two jet at a point as a symmetric coefficient matrix A, a first-order vector b and a zeroth-order scalar c. Stabilizer rotations diag(1,-1,-1) and diag(-1,1,-1) force the off-diagonal coefficients and b to vanish; quarter-turns about coordinate axes force the three diagonal entries equal. Conversely A=aI,b=0 is invariant under every rotation. Transitivity therefore gives a multiple of the metric Laplacian plus a constant, with no invariant first-order remainder. The scalar zero-mode convention removes that constant. On scalar harmonic degree k the two chiral Casimirs each have j(j+1), j=k/2, so 2(C_L+C_R)/R^2=k(k+2)/R^2, checking the retained radius normalization. The corrected proof and original scalar theorem are verified at their stated R>0 scope.

BH-IID-EV-UPDATE-E3-G004

The revised statement and proof explicitly attach the displayed squared pair to the two original retained k0 spinor sectors, and explicitly deny that they must remain the lowest full smooth-spinor values for arbitrary real m. This exactly matches the operator calculation. For every real m, the spin perturbation (m/R)I is local, self-adjoint and Spin(4)-equivariant, is zeroth order and commutes with every scalar multiplication operator. It is bounded for fixed R>0 and preserves the self-adjoint Dirac domain. Consequently the principal symbol and coordinate commutators are unchanged.

The original retained spinor eigenvalues are ±3/(2R), so on those same sectors the shifted squares are (m±3/2)^2/R^2 for every real m. At m=3/2 the original negative k0 sector is zero; at m=-3/2 the original positive k0 sector is zero. Each sector has complex dimension two. Hence the retained scalar zero space acquires an additional spinor summand, while the canonical m0 retained square has only its scalar zero line. This proves the main no-rigidity conclusion without requiring any global eigenvalue ordering.

The previous full-parent ordering witness is now consistent with the printed qualifier: R1,m5/2 gives retained squares16,1, while the full negative k1 mode shifts from -5/2 to0. The updated statement allows precisely this situation. It does not discard that higher mode, weaken the main no-go, or assert a new physical vacuum/Hamiltonian owner. Thus the corrected source-as-printed statement and proof are verified for all real m, and the prior ordering objection no longer applies.

No verdict was inferred from an audit status flag or from a script that merely reprints statuses. The evidence is the explicit tangent-action, jet and spectral-shift calculations above. No source/canonical graph edit, new mechanism or new theorem was produced by this review.
